Burn Like A Dragon, Rise Like A Phoenix
by MrMattimation
Summary

Haruka Sawamura is a woman on a mission with a family to provide for.
Kazuma Kiryu has been dead for six years, and in that time, Haruka Sawamura has taken over the
Morning Glory orphanage, following in his footsteps by taking on a new generation of orphans.
After the death of her husband, she journeys alone to the Isezaki Ijincho ward of Yokohama to
locate a businessman by the name of Ichiban Kasuga so that she can secure funding for the future
of the orphanage.
When she arrives, however, she finds that Kasuga is nowhere to be found, and what's worse, one of
the city's largest criminal factions seems to want her dead. But Haruka is a difficult woman to scare
off. Determined to provide a better future for the orphans and for her own son, Haruka proceeds
undeterred, and soon finds herself knee-deep in a criminal conspiracy that spans the whole of Japan
and threatens the wellbeing of her entire family. With the help of some new friends made along the
way, as well as some old faces from her past, she tries to get to the bottom of it all - and makes a
shocking discovery relating to the truth behind Kiryu's death.
A "what-if" story set between Yakuza: Like A Dragon and Like A Dragon Infinite Wealth.

Chapter 1: Prologue
Sōtenbori, Osaka, Japan
December 15th, 2022
It was a chilly and crowded December evening in Osaka’s Sōtenbori district. The air was slightly
colder this night than was normal for this part of Japan, but this didn’t do much to discourage the
nightlife. Droves of people crowded all up and down the district, coming and going from the
various shops, restaurants, bars, and cabaret clubs that lined the streets. Still more people arrived by
the minute from elsewhere in Osaka; business was booming.
Not all were here for pleasure, however; on the eastern end of Sotenbori Street, a cab arrived at the
taxi stand, its passenger having just arrived from the airport.
“Here is fine,” the passenger, a woman in her mid twenties, said as the taxi pulled up to the stand.
“Thank you.” She paid the fare - about ¥7000, an amount she hated to part with considering the
circumstances - and stepped out of the vehicle. She had shoulder-length black hair, tied back in a
ponytail, with the front combed forward into a set of bangs, and was dressed casually, wearing a
white hoodie over a red undershirt, a short denim skirt, and ankle-high brown boots. Over her face
was a blue 3-ply medical face mask, worn not for health concerns as most in this day and age
would, but in order to conceal her identity.
After all, this wasn’t the first time Haruka Sawamura had been to Osaka.
She had been out of the public spotlight for more than a decade at this point. Other idols had come
and gone in that time, and with a career as short as hers - starting and ending with a single concert
at the Japan Dome nearly ten years ago to the day - most of the older population in Japan had likely
forgotten all about her, and the kids had probably never heard of her. But the chances that she
would be recognized, by a fan or otherwise, were never zero, especially in Osaka, and Haruka
wanted to avoid any complications.
She had a lot of memories in this city. She hadn’t been back here since just after the Princess
League, when she had been forced to flee to Tokyo upon being embroiled in a conspiracy involving
the Omi Alliance, a Kansai-based yakuza organization that, once-upon-a-time, controlled the city
with an iron grip. Despite that, not all of these memories were bad ones. It was here that she
learned the art of the dance battle. She made new friends here she wouldn’t have otherwise. And, if
only for a moment, the now-defunct Dyna Chair talent management company allowed her to live
her dream in front of thousands of people.
Really, only one thing was missing from her life back then… and just when she had him back, he
was ripped away from her again. Permanently.
“To me… Kazuma Kiryu is family.”
But she couldn’t dwell on that now. She had people back home in Okinawa depending on her. With
that in mind, she started to make her way to her destination. She didn’t walk very long, however,
before bumping into a group of very drunk businessmen who were stumbling through the street.
She grunted after their collision - the man she bumped into was so drunk, he could barely stand up
straight, and fell onto the ground.

“Oh!” Haruka exclaimed. “I’m so sorry, mister! Please excuse me!”
“Hey!” the man yelled, struggling to get back up. “Why don’tcha watch where yer goin?!” he
slurred heavily.
“Sorry!”
The man stood fully up, stared at Haruka, then his frown turned into a smile. “Ah… yer a pretty
face… ain’t she, boys?” He turned to his friends, who nodded, then he turned back to Haruka. “I
bet it’s even prettier once ya take the mask off… and, well, some other stuff, too. Tell me
somethin’… ya got yerself a man?”
Haruka cringed. Yup, she was in Sotenbori. “Excuse me. I have to go,” she said as she attempted to
remove herself from the situation.
“Hey! Weren’t ya taught it’s rude to ignore yer elders?!” the man exclaimed, grabbing Haruka’s
wrist.
“Ah!”
“Now, listen, you bumped into me! I could be hurt real bad! But I’m willin’ ta look past all that…
Why don’tcha come out for drinks with me an’ my pals?”
“I think you’ve had enough,” she said, struggling to get free.
“Heh… what’s the matter? Don’tcha wanna have a little fun with us…?” he slurred, getting entirely
too close to Haruka. “What’re ya hiding under here, anyway?” He reached up and grabbed
Haruka’s breast.
Glaring at the man, Haruka knee'd the man in the groin. He groaned, let go of her wrist, and fell
onto the floor. “I’m sorry,” Haruka apologized. “But I have somewhere to be.” She started to walk
away.
“Hey, bitch!” one of the man’s friends called out. Haruka sighed and turned back to face them…
and saw that one of them had pulled out a knife. “Where do ya think you’re going?! That was
mighty rude of ya! Do ya know who yer messin’ with, here?!”
Haruka backed up from them. “I’d really just like to go,” she pleaded.
“It’s a bit late for that!” the man with the knife yelled. “Ya could’ve come back with us, had a fun
evening! Now ya gotta get cut!”
“Let her go,” a deep-voiced man said from behind the knife-wielding thugs. The men turned around
and stared at the man addressing them. Tall and rather handsome for his age, the black-haired man
stood before them in a red suit jacket with a black button up shirt underneath, buttoned only up to
his chest.
“Akiyama-san!” Haruka exclaimed.
“This don’t concern you, pal!” the leader said, standing back up after Haruka’s punch to the gut.
“Or do ya wanna get cut too?”

Haruka’s defender, one Shun Akiyama, smirked. “You’re causing a scene. Has anybody told you
that rarely ends well in this town?"
“Oh yeah? Says who?” the man laughed. “Ever since the Omi Alliance skipped town, we’ve been
able to do whatever the hell we want! And then those lockdowns a couple of years back made bein’
a yakuza mighty unprofitable, so whatever was left closed up shop. It’s open season out here,
now!”
Akiyama chuckled. “It’s not the yakuza you need to worry about these days,” he said, before
launching into a series of kicks that knocked the man down. His ally with the knife ran at Akiyama.
Akiyama kicked the knife out of his hand, then delivered a powerful blow to his chest that knocked
him over. He then stomped on the man’s face, causing him to lose a few teeth in the process, and
the man passed out. The last punk realized he was screwed, and fearfully turned and ran away,
apologizing as he did so.
“I gotta say,” Akiyama said once the coast was clear, “fighting these guys used to be a lot more fun
when the yakuza were still in town. At least they were tough.” He turned to Haruka and smiled at
her. “You know it’s dangerous at night, Haruka-chan,” he chided.
Haruka smiled back at him, and nodded. “Yeah. I know. I’m trying to be careful.”
“What brings you to Sotenbori, anyway?” Akiyama asked. “Shouldn’t you be down in Okinawa?”
“Oh, Ayako is taking care of things in my absence,” Haruka replied, referring to her foster sister
who now helped her manage the Morning Glory orphanage in Okinawa. “She’s watching over
Haruto, too. I don’t plan to be gone very long. Actually, I came here hoping to speak with you, so
it’s good luck you showed up. I had heard you re-opened.”
Akiyama frowned. “Why? You’re not looking for a loan, are you?”
Haruka sighed. “Can we go to your office, please, Akiyama-san?”
“Uh… yeah. Yeah, right this way.”
***
Sky Finance Sotenbori was as messy as Haruka remembered it. Boxes and empty beer cans and
ramen bowls were stacked up on the desks and shelves. The drawers looked like they had no
organization system in place. The ashtray on the coffee table was full of cigarette butts. It looked
like a hoarder lived here. Not that Haruka really minded. It was just who Akiyama was. “Please,
have a seat,” Akiyama offered, gesturing to the two couches sitting across from each other, a coffee
table in between. “Please excuse the mess. I haven’t gotten a chance to tidy up.”
“Would you have tidied up if you did have a chance?” Haruka shot back, smirking as she sat down.
“Ahh! You wound me, Haruka-chan. But no. I suppose not.” Akiyama sat down across from her.
“Now then. Why is it you came to see me?”
Haruka frowned. “Well… to be honest with you, Akiyama-san, things haven’t been great at the
orphanage since Uncle Kaz passed,” she explained. “Things were fine, for a while. Everyone
pitched in and helped out. Yuta and I raised Haruto together… after the Tojo Clan and Omi
Alliance disbanded, Daigo Dojima came by the orphanage and offered him a position at his new

security company for ex-yakuza, so he was able to go completely straight. It meant that Haruto
didn’t get to see his father as much, as the company is based here in Osaka, but his job kept us fed
and kept the orphanage running and he was with us as much as he could be. We, um… we had even
been trying for another baby,” she said, blushing slightly.
Akiyama frowned. “Where is Yuta-san now?”
“Dead,” Haruka said. “Almost two years ago, now.”
Hearing this caused Akiyama to sigh. “Oh, Haruka-chan,” he said. “I’m so sorry.”
“He became very ill around Christmas, and by February he was… gone.” Haruka wiped a tear from
her eye.
“And he was so young, too…” Akiyama sighed. “How’s Haruto holding up?”
Haruka sniffled. “He’s doing well. Of course, when you’re that young… I doubt he’ll even
remember who his father was, which is…” she couldn’t finish that thought. What she was saying
was absolutely terrible. The two men Haruto owed his life to were gone, and he was going to grow
up not knowing who they even were. She started to break down. Akiyama let her cry for a minute,
before Haruka calmed herself.
“Well… anyway, after he passed, the money he was sending every month dried up. We had been
receiving money anonymously from… someone else as well, washed through a bunch of different
accounts… We had a private investigator with a Kamurocho detective agency look into it. Takayuki
Yagami, maybe you’ve heard of him?”
“A little,” Akiyama replied. “He hasn’t been seen around Tokyo lately though. His gorilla-looking
partner’s been handling business since the start of the year.”
“Well, according to him, the trail ended at the account of a government official by the name of
Minoru Daidoji, who’s been dead since at least 2017… and as soon as we figured that out, the
money stopped coming, like they didn’t want us to know who was behind it. The whole thing was
very strange, but it didn’t change the end result… we weren’t receiving any money anymore.
“Things have been very tight since then. If we don’t figure something out soon, I’ll need to close
Morning Glory, and I don’t know where the children will be able to go.”
“How many?”
“Um, minus Haruto, there’s six of them,” Haruka said as she started to list them off. “From oldest
to youngest, there’s Akira, Sakura, Makio, Yoko, Makoto, and… Yumi. It was a funny coincidence,
when she came to us. Yumi was my mother’s name. And the oldest boy, Akira, shares a given name
with Uncle Kaz’s sworn brother, Nishikiyama. It feels like… I was meant to take care of them.”
Haruka paused, then continued. “One night, when I was 12 or 13, Uncle Kaz and I sat on the beach,
and he told me stories about his life before prison… what Nishikiyama and my mother were like
back then, too. Actually, the strangest thing about it was that he recalled it all so fondly, even
though it all came to such a bad end. And I got the sense that he felt like everything that happened
after that… like it was his fault somehow. It was as if he felt… that he had failed them.

“And so when these children came into my care, I knew I had to make sure they had the best lives I
could give them. Not just for them, but for Uncle Kaz. In some weird way, it’s like I’m making up
for the mistakes of the past this way. Hopefully it’ll help him rest easy.” Haruka smiled at Akiyama.
“So… I need to borrow some money. Mitsuo just signed with the Nagoya Wyverns. He’s going to
be sending money soon. But until that money comes, we’re in a bit of a bad spot.”
Akiyama thought about it. “Hmm. Kiryu-san wouldn’t want you getting involved with a loan shark,
Haruka-chan.”
“You’re not a loan shark,” Haruka pointed out. “No credit checks. No interest. No collateral. That’s
how Sky Finance operates. And I’ll pay back every yen. I just need it to get us through the next few
months.”
“How much?”
“Five million yen.”
“That’s not a small amount, Haruka. That’s a year’s wages in Okinawa… maybe a little more.”
“You’ve given out more than that. Whatever we don’t use will come right back to you, and then the
rest will be paid back monthly.”
Akiyama sighed. “Hmmm… you do know that my loans aren’t completely no-strings, right? There
is one prerequisite.”
Haruka nodded. “You’re going to give me a test. Whatever it is, Akiyama-san… I’m going to give
it my all, and I’m going to pass, so the children can live the lives they deserve!”
Akiyama chuckled. “I would expect nothing less. Well, if you’re sure…” He leaned back and
thought about what his test would be. “Hmmm… now what exactly would be a good test for
you…?”
“Whatever it is, I can do it,” Haruka replied.
“Careful,” Akiyama warned. “Some of my tests are pretty out-there.”
“And I’m willing to do whatever it takes. I’ll- I’ll even work in one of your cabaret clubs!”
Akiyama was surprised at this. “No,” he said firmly. “Kiryu-san would kick my ass from beyond
the grave if I made you do that.”
“I used to work in one."
“Seriously?!” Akiyama exclaimed.
Haruka nodded. “I worked at one in town when money first started getting tight. I can do that kind
of work if you need me to.”
“Tch. You’re not a little girl anymore, huh…” It was difficult to believe that she was closer to thirty
than twenty at this point. She looked almost exactly like she did when she was 16, and though the
stress of motherhood had clearly aged her somewhat, Akiyama couldn’t picture her in any other
light. Still, he refused. “Nope. Off the table.”

“Okay then.” Truthfully, that was a bit of a relief for Haruka. Her gimmick during her brief stint as
a hostess was that she was… disgraced former teen idol Haruka Sawamura. That was not one of her
best ideas.
Akiyama snapped his fingers. “I got it. Haruka-chan, have you been to Yokohama?”
Haruka tilted her head. “Yokohama? Um, once, I think, when I was little…” And had been
kidnapped. “But I didn’t get to see very much of it. I was… a little tied up with other things.”
Akiyama started looking around for something. “Crap. Where is that business card… uh… aha!”
He grabbed it from underneath a beer can and handed it to Haruka. “There’s this guy. Ichiban
Kasuga. Some former Tojo Clan grunt, got arrested at the turn of the century, I don’t really know a
whole lot about that. He left the business a while back, and now he’s running a more legitimate
business.”
“Kasuga…?” Haruka muttered, reading the business card, which appeared to be for a company
called Ichiban Holdings. “He was in the Tojo Clan? Do you think Uncle Kaz would have known
him?”
Akiyama shook his head. “Not likely. The way I hear it, this guy and Kiryu were never really on the
streets at the same time, and they were in different families, anyway. Kasuga was in the Arakawa
Family, while Kiryu worked for Sohei Dojima. In 1995, Kiryu goes to prison, then Kasuga does as
well in 2001, and four years later Kiryu’s sentence is up. Kasuga leaves prison in 2019, by which
point… Well, you get the idea. Anyway. His company, Ichiban Holdings? Coincidentally, they’re
looking to expand into Okinawa. They want to use it as a foothold to expand into the United States,
or so I hear.”
Haruka nodded. “It makes sense, I suppose,” she said. “There’s a lot of US military in Okinawa, so
he’d have a lot of American customers down there.”
“Right,” Akiyama affirmed, nodding. “Of course, he’s going to need partners down there to give
him good standing in the community. Do you see where I’m going with this?”
“I think so,” Haruka said slowly.
“Simply put, I don’t think borrowing money for the rest of your life is a sustainable way to run the
orphanage,” Akiyama explained. “And if Mitsuo’s baseball career doesn’t end up working out,
you’ll be back in here looking to borrow more in no time. If, however, Morning Glory had financial
backing from a successful Japanese organization… well, you wouldn’t have to worry as much
anymore.”
“I suppose that makes sense,” Haruka mused, a finger on her chin. “Sunflower had funding from
the Tojo Clan until Kazama-san died. I don’t think Uncle Kaz would have wanted money coming in
from a yakuza organization… but you said Kasuga-san isn't a yakuza anymore, right?”
“Right. So here’s your test…” Akiyama leaned back, smiling. “I want you to go to Yokohama and
convince Kasuga-san to sign a long-term financial partnership with Morning Glory. Do that, and
I’ll give you the five million.”
“But then I won’t need the five million,” Haruka pointed out.

“Call it a bonus,” Akiyama replied. “Look, even if you get his signature, it’ll take time for that deal
to get set up, so you’re gonna need a cash injection to get started. Whatever you spend it on isn’t
really my business. Renovations, repairs… bathe in it… I don’t really care.”
“Bathe in it?” Haruka asked, tilting her head.
“A lot of weirdos come in here,” Akiyama sighed. “Well. Anyway. Are those terms acceptable to
you?”
Haruka let out a big smile and nodded. “Yes! Absolutely!” She stood up and bowed. “Thank you so
much, Akiyama-san!”
Akiyama chuckled. “Hmph. Don’t thank me just yet. You don’t have the money yet.”
“Sorry, I know I’m getting carried away,” Haruka admitted, wiping a tear from her eye. “These last
few years have been hard. But I’m going to give it my all! I’ll be on the first train to Yokohama
tomorrow!"
Akiyama noticed something on her wrist as she wiped the tear away. It looked like… “Sorry,
Haruka. Is that a tattoo?”
“Huh? Oh! Oh, yes,” Haruka said, pushing her left sleeve up. “Just a small one. I got it done a few
years ago by the artist who did Uncle Kaz’s, back in Kamurocho.” It was indeed quite a small
tattoo - most probably wouldn’t notice it. A Chinese dragon wrapped around her wrist like a
bracelet. Midway through, the dragon became engulfed in flames, and what appeared to be a
phoenix emerged from the other end. “I know they’re still taboo, but a small one like this won’t
turn any heads. I don’t really visit any onsen or any places like that, and… I want to keep his
memory with me always.”
“The design hasn’t been filled in, yet,” Akiyama commented.
“I haven’t been back to Tokyo since the lockdowns. And I don’t want just any artist to fill it in. I
want Kiryu’s artist to fill it in. Speaking of… Akiyama-san. What made you decide to reopen in
Sotenbori, rather than Kamurocho?”
Akiyama gave her a very serious look. “Kamurocho’s a very different place ever since the yakuza
left town,” he explained. “And after Governor Aoki was assassinated, crime shot up.”
“Oh, yeah, I heard about that…” Haruka muttered. Ryo Aoki, the Governor of Tokyo. He was the
reason the Tojo Clan were forced to leave Kamurocho with his Kamurocho 3K Plan. He was also
the co-founder of Bleach Japan, a socio-political movement to wipe Japan free of crime and crimeadjacent gray zones. But his disciple, Sota Kume, assassinated him shortly after the 2019 elections,
around the same time it became known that Aoki was actually the son of the Acting Captain of the
Omi Alliance, Masumi Arakawa. The resulting fallout caused the Citizens’ Liberal Party to fall out
of public favor, and they lost their governing majority after the Prime Minister called for an early
election. Kume’s family publicly described Bleach Japan as a cult that ruined his life, garnering a
great deal of media attention, and the Supreme Court has been considering a ban on Bleach Japan
activities since then.
“I would rather be there than here,” Akiyama said. “But it’s not safe there anymore. So do me a
favor when you get back to Kanto… stay away from Kamurocho. At least for now. Okay?”

Haruka nodded. “Okay. Thank you.” With that, she turned and left. As the door closed, Akiyama
chuckled and lit a cigarette.
“Hmph… Kiryu-san…” he muttered to nobody in particular. “Whatever shadows you’re hiding
in… there are people in the sunlight who still need you.”

Chapter 2: Isezaki Ijincho
Chapter Summary

In which an idol and a barmaid walk into a bar.

The ocean waves crashed along the beach, providing a consistent white noise that soothed Haruka
as she sat and watched the sunset. She thought about everything that had happened to her lately,
amazed that she’d been able to make it through it all. All of it was finally coming to an end… or
she hoped, anyway.
“Hey, Haruka,” an older male voice said behind her.
Haruka looked up to see who was addressing her. “Oh, Uncle Kaz!” she greeted, standing up.
Standing before her was her adoptive father.
Kazuma Kiryu. Ex-Tojo Clan Fourth Chairman.
He was a somewhat tall, muscular man with spiked up black hair, wearing white dress pants, brown
dress shoes, and a slightly tacky red and white leaf-pattern Kariyushi shirt. His face was grumpy,
but Haruka never felt intimidated or threatened by it; he wasn’t really grumpy, he just looked that
way.
“Your dinner is getting cold,” Kiryu announced. “Is everything okay?”
Haruka nodded. “Yeah. I’ll be back inside soon. I’m just… thinking about everything we’ve been
through this past year.”
“With Hamazaki, you mean?”
Haruka grew silent. She sat back down and stared out at the ocean again. Kiryu came over and sat
next to her.
“Haruka… it’s over, now,” he said. “I’m still around, and Hamazaki’s in prison. You don’t have
anything to worry about.”
“I was… so afraid of losing you,” Haruka said. “What he did to you… I’ll never be able to forgive
him. I won’t ever forget it.”
Kiryu stared at her with his usual intense stare. “That’s dangerous,” he said finally.
“Huh?”
“Holding grudges like that,” Kiryu explained. “It’s not good for you. And if left to fester long
enough, it can drive someone to do something regrettable.”

“And that’s why Hamazaki did what he did, right?” Haruka asked. “He tried to kill you because of
a grudge.”
Kiryu nodded. “Yeah. But… I’m speaking from more personal experience than that.”
Haruka looked up at him. “Uncle Kaz?”
“I come from a very dangerous and deadly world, Haruka,” Kiryu explained. “Some leave in a box.
Some get thrown in jail. And some, like me, can get out and try and live some semblance of a
normal life… but nobody leaves the yakuza unscathed. And nobody leaves innocent or with clean
hands either. That’s just how it is in the life I chose to lead.”
“But you’re not like the others.”
Kiryu raised an eyebrow. “I’m not? That’s news to me,” he said. “The truth is, Haruka… I’ve never
been a saint. I can hide from my past all I want. But no matter how much I hate it… I’ll always be
yakuza.”
Haruka looked down at the ground. “What are you saying?”
“I’m saying that Hamazaki and I aren’t that different,” Kiryu sighed. “So I know why he did what
he did.”
“Have you ever… you know?” Haruka asked.
Kiryu was silent for a moment. Finally, he replied, saying, “The things I’ve done have never been
in cold blood, or out of hatred,” he said, not really fully answering the question.
“So then that means you’re not like Hamazaki,” Haruka said firmly. “No matter what you’ve had to
do, you’re a good person. He’s not.”
“Except… for one time,” Kiryu finished.
“Huh?”
“I was young. Very young,” he explained. “I was still green, working my way up in the Dojima
Family… although, back then I wasn’t in their good graces. I had been on the run from them, too
deep in a conspiracy I had no business being involved in. But… somebody needed my help.”
Haruka smiled. “Wow. Even back then, you couldn’t help getting involved when people were in
trouble.”
“Heh,” Kiryu chuckled. “I can’t stand by when people need my help, no. But… back then I had yet
to understand what it meant to be a yakuza. Honestly, I hadn’t even earned the dragon on my back.
So when I finally came face-to-face with the man responsible for everything…” Kiryu fell silent.
“Did you…?” Haruka asked slowly.
“I would have,” Kiryu answered. “Had it not been for Nishiki.”
“Nishikiyama?” Haruka asked, confused.
“Yeah. He was my sworn brother,” Kiryu said, letting out a rare smile. “I’ve told you that, right?”

Haruka nodded. “Mhm. You said that you grew up at Sunflower together. You, him… and mom.”
“Yeah. He was the one who stopped me from ending the man’s life,” Kiryu explained. “I’d have
done it if he hadn’t been there. I’d have crossed a line you can’t come back from.”
“Nishikiyama stopped you?” Haruka asked. It was almost hard to believe that the men Haruka saw
duke it out with her own eyes used to be so different… or that there was a line Kiryu was willing to
cross that Nishikiyama couldn’t. “So… he saved you?”
“Exactly,” Kiryu affirmed, nodding. “He told me… if there ever came a time that I had to cross that
line… he’d be there to cross it with me. I decided the man I hated wasn't worth making Nishiki
cross that line with me. It’s because of him that I am who I am today.”
“Do you miss him?”
Kiryu sighed. “Every day.”
They were both silent for a bit after that. Finally, Haruka spoke up. “Do you blame me for what
happened?”
Kiryu looked at her. “Why would I blame you?”
“Well… I came into your life… and then you lost everyone important to you.” She hugged her legs
close to her body and stared out towards the ocean. “It’s because of me that—”
“Haruka… Nishiki’s fall started before you were even born,” Kiryu explained. “If anybody is to
blame for the way things turned out, it’s me. I wasn’t there for him the same way he was for me.
That will always be my greatest failure. After everything that happened, I was almost ready to give
up. I was going to go back to prison. Might even have died there.”
Kiryu turned to Haruka and smiled. “But then I realized… I did have one thing still going for me.
That was you. As long as I had you… I had a reason to keep going. When I went into prison, the
hope that I might see Nishiki and Yumi again was what kept me moving forward. And after it was
all over, taking care of you became my new responsibility.” He looked up at the sky. “Maybe if
Hamazaki had somebody like you in his life… things would have turned out different. We’re all
victims of circumstance, Haruka. Remember that.”
Haruka nodded. “Okay. I’ll try.”
***
Haruka awoke from her slumber right as her train was beginning to approach Jinnai Station in
Yokohama’s Isezaki Ijincho district, having fallen asleep somewhere during the nearly three hour
journey from Osaka to here. Truth be told, she hadn’t been sleeping very much at all, lately. With
things so difficult, it became hard to get any rest, but with an end to her worries in sight, suddenly
she couldn’t wait to get back to Okinawa so she could pass out and sleep for three days straight.
This would’ve been unthinkable when she was younger and full of energy, but she was not nine
anymore. Sometimes, Haruka worried that the way she lived her life—constantly in danger, though
not really through any fault of her own—was prematurely aging her, and the added stress of
deciding to open Morning Glory to new orphans when she really didn’t have the money to do so
definitely wasn’t helping. Still, she knew that it would all be over soon.

But I always think that, she thought to herself as the train came to a complete stop and she stood up.
And then… something happens. But, she also knew that the adversity she faced in her life made her
stronger for having experienced and overcome it all.
And that was what she needed. She needed to be stronger. She was in constant peril from childhood
until she was a mother, and eventually, it’s what got her dear Uncle Kaz killed. Had she not been
kidnapped in Onomichi…
She shook the thought away as she stepped off the train. No use thinking about that now, she told
herself. Kiryu had given his life so that she could live hers with her family. Yuta was gone now, but
she still had Haruto, and she knew damn well Kiryu wouldn’t have wanted her living with that guilt
when she had people depending on her.
With that being said, she needed to find Ichiban Holdings and speak to this Ichiban Kasuga so that
she could secure a bright future for Haruto and the orphans at Morning Glory. Fortunately, based on
the address Akiyama had given her, the company headquarters wasn’t that far from the station, so
she decided to walk the rest of the distance. She typed the address into the GPS on her phone and
started the final stretch of her journey.
After she typed the address in, she noticed a new email that she’d apparently received during the
train ride.
From: Mack.Shinozuka
To: SunflowerDragonPrincess; DQHero; Suzuki.T; and 9 others
Subject: Revealing Your Calling with Revelations!
Yo! It’s Mack again!
Ever feel like you don’t have a place in this world? Good news; it exists! You just haven’t found it
yet.
Watch people on the street. See what they do. If you find something interesting, you may just have a
REVELATION, and an idea for a new job will come to you just like that!
If you find something, be sure to post about it on my new photo sharing site, Macstagram! You just
might inspire someone else to take on a new job!
In smaller text at the bottom, the email also read:
You received this email because you were subscribed to a mailing list. Click here to unsubscribe.
Haruka frowned as she read the email. She’d been getting spam emails from this guy for at least a
decade. I really should block him, she thought to herself as she closed the email and continued on
her way.

The walk to the set of office buildings Ichiban Holdings was headquartered in was quick enough

death, there did still appear to be triads here, but none of them bothered her, so she didn’t pay them

“Isezaki Ijincho is divided up into three territories by three gangs,” Akiyama explained. “If you

“First, we have the Yokohama Liumang, centered around Chinatown. They originally fought with
the Snake Flower Triad for the territory, but back in 2009, Lau Ka Long was killed in Kamurocho

Snake Flower were, but they’re dangerous all the same. They were led by Tianyou Zhao, but in

“Next, we have the Seiryu Clan, Ijincho’s local yakuza. Their influence has grown since the Tojo
Clan disbanded, but they still mostly operate in and around Yokohama.”
“They have territory in Tokyo now, too,” Haruka commented. “Yuta had a run-in with them on a

Akiyama nodded. “They’ve got a few subsidiary families now. I hear they’re planning to move in

“Their previous chairman was assassinated by some Omi Alliance breakaways back in 2019. He

Haruka nodded. “Got it.”

The cab dropped Haruka off just across from Survive Bar. “Thank you,” she said as she paid the

Haruka approached the bar and sat down next to the woman, who appeared to have already

Chapter 3: Yokohama Crackhouse
Chapter Summary

Haruka learns to fight and Saeko learns an uncomfortable secret.

How do I get into these situations? Haruka thought to herself as she and Saeko braced themselves
for attack.
The two women were up against four assailants from the Yokohama Liumang, two of whom
wielded blades. Saeko seemed to be utilizing her handbag as a weapon, but as Haruka wasn’t
exactly expecting to get into any fights, she was stuck with her fists.
Saeko looked over at her. “Hey. You can do this. Just take your time and think about your attack.
There’s no shame in taking a few hits if it means you can hit them where you know it hurts. Icchan
— ugh. Somebody who shall remain nameless once told me it’s easier if you think about it like a
video game.”
“A video game…?” Haruka asked.
“Yeah. I thought it was stupid as hell too. But… It works. Trust me on this.”
Haruka nodded. “Okay.”
“Here, I’ll go first. Watch and learn.” Saeko glared at their assailants and attacked, running at one
of them with her handbag and hitting him with it. She followed this up with a swift kick at his
ankles, tripping him and sending him crashing to the ground. He didn’t get back up.
“Whoa!” Haruka exclaimed.
Saeko smiled at her. “See? Easy. Your turn!”
Haruka nodded and glared at one of the remaining Liumang. She didn’t know how to fight… but
she did know someone who did. She closed her eyes and tried to remember.
“If you want to die, then step up!”
Haruka opened her eyes and gasped. “I got it!” she exclaimed. She was having a REVELATION!
In her mind, she could see herself executing basic kicks and punches, emulating the brawler
fighting style of somebody very dear to her. Her memory was hazy, so these attacks wouldn’t be
very powerful, but it was a start.
She ran at the enemy in front of her and threw two light punches, followed by a finishing punch to
his nose, which sent him to the ground.

“Nice one!” Saeko congratulated. “Doesn’t really seem like your style, but it works. For now,

~Where Do You Hang Your Hat?~
As Haruka and Saeko walked together towards Geomijul, Haruka looked around and took in the

“Well, I am a mother, so…”

Captain Sano stood at the window in his new office at the Seiryu Clan Tokyo Branch headquarters.
From here, he had a magnificent view of the palace grounds, Mt. Fuji, and the Shinjuku skyline,

would ever expand outside of Ijincho, but here he was, captain of its Tokyo branch. Soon, they
would move on Shinjuku, more specifically its red light district of Kamurocho, in large numbers,
and reestablish the order that was shattered when the Tojo Clan left Tokyo.
But tonight, he was content admiring the skyline.
Sano was an ambitious man, but he was also a pragmatic man. The Seiryu Clan had grown, but had
they grown large enough to effectively wrest control of the city from the street gangs that ravaged
it? He thought not. They certainly couldn’t do so as a divided clan, and divided they certainly
would be if that arrogant jackass Ebina had his way. If it weren’t for that idiot Mitsuo Kiryu taking
the heat for the intrusion on the Yokohama Seiryu’s turf, Ebina would already be on his way out
and there would be nothing threatening Sano’s vision—a vision he shared with the chairman.
Sano heard his door open. “Eh?” he grunted as he turned to face it. “I’m busy. Who’s disturbing me
at this hour—?” He didn’t get a chance to see who had entered before he felt a tanto drive itself
straight into his gut. “Urk!” he groaned in pain as the intruder sliced him open, blood spraying onto
his desk and covering much of his daily paperwork, money, even a photo of his loved ones. The
intruder then withdrew the blade from his gut and kicked him, sending him crashing out of the
window and landing on the pavement below.
He died on impact, and his corpse laid there in a slowly growing pool of its own blood. It was a
violent and abrupt end for the last of the honorable yakuza, and the beginning of the end for the
Seiryu Clan.

“This is Yagami,” the voice on the other end greeted.
“Hey, Tak, it’s me. Listen, don’t come back to Kamurocho right now. Keep your ass in Sotenbori
until I give you the all clear. Shit’s all fucked up right now, and I don’t know how I’m gonna fix it,
because I gotta lay low for a bit.”
“Did something happen, Kaito-san?” Yagami asked.
“Yeah. The captain of the Seiryu Clan’s dead,” Kaito explained. “Murdered. And right now, I’m a
prime suspect. So I’m going off the grid for a bit until I get this shit figured out, and you should
probably do the same.”

“Damn, we just can’t catch a break, can we?” Yagami chuckled. “After all that shit went down in
Yokohama last year, too… Alright. I’ll lay low for a bit. I trust you’ve got this handled?”
Kaito couldn’t help but laugh. “Trying my best. I could use some help though. See, the other
suspect is this girl. Fuck, Tak, she made shit worse for herself just to give me a chance to escape,
she didn’t even know me. Why’d she have to go and do that? Agh… Anyway. Her name’s Haruka
Sawamura. You took a case for her, right?”
Yagami thought about it. “Yeah, I think so. She runs that orphanage in Okinawa. She wanted the
source of some money traced.”
“And you traced it to a guy named…?”
“Daidoji.”

“Likewise.” Kaito hung up the phone, and sighed. “Oh, man… what a mess…”

Chapter 13: The Idol at Rock Bottom
Haruka sat alone at a cold metal desk in a cold, sterile, featureless interrogation room. Across from
her was an empty seat, intended for the police officer who would be coming soon to question her.
Behind that chair was a single door, next to which was a mirror, which she guessed from watching
crime dramas on TV was actually a one-way window. She’d been in here for what she guessed was
about forty minutes, though she couldn’t know that for sure as the room also had no clock and her
cellphone had been confiscated. Her only companion the entire time was the consistent hum of the
fluorescent lights in the ceiling above her. She sighed again. Am I ever getting out of here? she
wondered to herself.
Just then, a detective entered the room. He was a tall, middle-aged man with short black hair and
wrinkles around his eyes and a cigarette in his mouth. He wore a blue suit, unbuttoned, with a light
blue dress shirt and a black tie. As he looked at Haruka, he reached up to grab the cigarette from his
mouth. When he did so, Haruka observed that he also wore a pair of black leather gloves, an odd
fashion choice for a police interrogator. Sighing, he sat down across from her and placed his badge
on the table.
“Good evening, Haruka-san,” he greeted. “My name is Akio Yamamoto. I’m a detective with the
Kamuro police.”
“They wouldn’t let Date-san do this, huh?” Haruka chuckled dryly.
“Date is too close to the case. He can’t be involved.”
“Can I speak with him after?”
“Outside of his capacity as a police detective, yes,” Yamamoto nodded. “You have a few visitors,
actually.”
“Be honest with me… I’m not leaving here tonight, am I?”
Yamamoto didn’t immediately answer. He crossed his arms. “What were you doing in the Seiryu
Clan offices, Haruka-san?”
“I was trying to warn Sano-san about a threat on his life,” she answered. “Mister, you have to
listen. I didn’t kill him.”
“So you wanted to warn him about a potential threat to his life… and you broke into his office to do
so?”
Haruka sighed. “I know it sounds hard to believe, but I couldn’t trust anybody else there, and with
good reason. Masataka Ebina killed him. Or Jo Sawashiro, on Ebina’s orders.”
Yamamoto’s face didn’t change. “What family are you with?” he asked.
“I’m not with any yakuza family.”
“Do me a favor. Roll up your sleeve.”

Haruka sighed, but did as she was told and rolled up her sleeve. She knew which one he was
talking about. He wanted to get a look at her tattoo.
“I’m sure you’re aware, Haruka, that dragons are a pretty big symbol in Tokyo’s criminal
underworld,” Yamamoto said.
“I’m sure you’d know,” Haruka replied. “You’re ex-yakuza, aren’t you?”
Yamamoto’s face faltered just a bit, but he didn’t seem too bothered by the assumption. “How do

“Your gloves,” Haruka pointed out. “You’re wearing them to hide a missing digit, right?”
Yamamoto was silent at first, but then nodded. “You’re pretty observant. Yes, as a youth, I was in a
small family out in Saitama. Made a mistake, lost my patriarch some money, paid the price for it.
Once, I wound up in trouble with the law. Pretty big trouble. However, the detective cut a deal with

“So you snitched,” Haruka deduced, a small hint of disgust in her tone. “Rather than face the

“I did what I had to. Blew the lid open on a big heist that was about to go down. Patriarch and

Haruka tilted her head. “How so?”
Yamamoto leaned back in his seat and sighed. “Thing is… as much of a media firestorm as it would

“We have probable cause to charge you. After that, it won’t be up to me. It’ll be up to a jury. One
that has heard of you before, Haruka Sawamura. There aren’t many in this country that haven’t.”

“Because, if you say the right thing… You might get off easy.”
“Huh?”
Yamamoto slid a photo across the table. It was of Kaito.
“This is Masaharu Kaito, formerly of the Tojo Clan’s Matsugane Family,” Yamamoto said. “He was

violent. And he’s at large.”
Haruka smiled. “So he got away, then.” Thank god.

“Do you know where he might’ve gone?” Yamamoto asked.
“What?”
“Well… If you helped us catch him… and you testified that he was the real mastermind, that he

Haruka glared at him. “Well, I hate to be the bearer of bad news, Yamamoto-san,” she began, “but I

Chapter End Notes

Trigger-free summary: Kasuga’s party and Taichi are meeting at a cafe to discuss their
findings relating to Mabuchi and the threat posed to Morning Glory. Taichi reveals he met
with Patriarch Nakahara of the Ryudo Family, who did not have relevant information, and asks
Zhao what he intends to do with Mabuchi. Zhao reveals to the party that he brought a handgun
to Okinawa, and that he plans to kill Mabuchi if he cannot be reasoned with, a plan which
Kasuga, Adachi, and Taichi all object to. It is made obvious through Zhao’s dialogue that he
does not wish to kill Mabuchi either.
Hanawa and another Daidoji agent, a young woman named Chihiro Watanabe who Taichi
takes a liking to, arrive and threaten Kasuga, which does not faze him; Chihiro takes on a
"good cop" persona and immediately hits it off with Taichi. During the discussion, the group is
attacked by several triads who taunt Zhao about Mabuchi. Kasuga urges Taichi to leave, but
Taichi refuses and fights alongside them. He fights using wrestling-influenced attacks, while
Chihiro fights with changquan.
After the battle, the triads reveal their links to the Saio Triad and claim they have no intent to
harm Haruto Sawamura, and then take their own lives before they can be further interrogated,
leaving the group to deal with the aftermath. With police on the way, Hanawa returns to a
Daidoji Faction safehouse, while the rest retreat to the Golden Dragon bar. Taichi joins the
party, as does Chihiro who does so under Hanawa’s orders to ensure Taichi’s safety.

Chapter 23: Closer
Taichi and Chihiro walked through the streets of Downtown Ryukyu, bored and looking for

Chapter 25: Morning Glory Road
Sugiura drove a lot faster than most were comfortable with, but probably about as fast as he needed
to, down the winding rural Okinawa roads towards Morning Glory Road, which straddled a beach
and a mountain in a remote part of the island. At some point, Kasuga had changed back into his
iconic red suit from his yakuza days, which he wore despite the island heat. “So, if you’re a
detective up in Ijincho, what are you doing here in Okinawa?” he asked.
“Well, if you’ve checked the news lately, you probably know that I’m a wanted man up in
Kanagawa,” Sugiura explained. “A few nights ago, right after Haruka Sawamura was arrested in
Tokyo, I got a call from Takayuki Yagami, who runs Yagami Detective Agency in Kamurocho. He
told me that his partner Kaito was on the run because of that, and that the police would probably be
coming for all of his associates. Wouldn’t you know it, minutes later, my partner Tsukumo hears on
a hacked police scanner that arrest warrants have been issued for all of us. Me, Yagami, Kaito,
Tsukumo—even our ex-yakuza acquaintance Higashi, and he runs an arcade for God’s sake. He
was pretty much out of the game even before the Great Dissolution. Apparently, they think we’re
all part of a massive plot to revive the Tojo Clan. They’re calling us the ‘Shin Tojo Alliance’ in the
media. As if I’d want anything to do with the yakuza.” He smirked at Kasuga. “Present company
excluded, of course.”
“So you guys got out of town before the police could even move on you,” Kasuga deduced,
nodding. “Smart.”
“Yup. Me and Tsukumo split up, because they were gonna be looking for a pair. Yagami was in
Sotenbori at the time on an unrelated case, so he’s staying there and laying low until things cool
down. No idea where Higashi and Kaito are, although I imagine two ex-yakuza know where to go
when things get nasty, so I’m not too worried about them.”
“So what made you come to Okinawa?” Adachi asked.
“Same reason you’re here,” Sugiura said. “Yagami told me that Kaito wanted him to look into
something called the Daidoji Faction, and that they seemed to have a particular interest in
Sawamura herself. So he asked me to come to Okinawa, where she lived, and see if I could turn
anything up here. No way I could turn down a trip to the beach. But, my search came up short…
Until I happened to hear about four jackasses from Yokohama who were causing all sorts of
problems for the local triads. Tracking you guys down seemed to be my best bet, and lo and behold,
we’re on our way to a Daidoji confrontation.”
Adachi raised an eyebrow. “How’d you get this far without cops scooping you up? Surely an APB
would’ve been sent out about you as soon as they realized you’d fled Yokohama, and you can’t get
to Okinawa without passing through some kind of ID checkpoint.”
Sugiura laughed. “Yeah. Everyone’s looking for Fumiya Sugiura. Unfortunately for the police,
Fumiya Sugiura doesn’t exist.” He pulled his wallet out and passed it to Kasuga. “Peep my ID.”
Kasuga grabbed his wallet and opened it.
Fumiya Terasawa
“Damn… They put an APB out on your alias? That’s kind of nuts.”

“Well, I haven’t used the name ‘Terasawa’ on anything in quite some time,” Sugiura chuckled,
although there was a hint of sadness in his voice. “Taichi, have you gotten in touch with anyone at
Morning Glory?”
Taichi shook his head. “Nobody’s picking up.”
“Well, it is dark,” Adachi said hopefully. “Maybe they’re just sleeping.”
“I sure hope so,” Sugiura said. “Anyway… We’re coming up on Morning Glory Road… oh, shit,”
he cursed as he slammed on his brakes.
Two black sedans had blocked the road, and several men in suits were standing in front of them.
Hanawa stood in the center of the group, smoking a cigarette. Sugiura’s car came to a stop about
fifty feet away from the roadblock.
“I imagine those guys are the Daidoji,” he said.
Kasuga nodded. “Yeah. Hey, I appreciate the ride… but I think this is as far as you go. You really
don’t wanna get involved with these guys. We’ll take it from here.”
Sugiura nodded. “I figured that’d be the case.”
“And as for the kid… take him back into town.”
Taichi looked at Kasuga. “What?”
“Sorry, Taichi-san,” Kasuga said as he and most of the others stepped out of the vehicle, with
Sugiura keeping Taichi’s door locked. Kasuga closed his door, and Sugiura locked that as well,
keeping the window rolled down so Kasuga could speak with Taichi. “But shit’s getting too
dangerous now. If you got hurt here, I don’t think I’d ever be able to face Kiryu-san… in this life,
or in any others.”
“No!” Taichi yelled, pulling on his door handle. “Hey, let me out!”
“Sorry, kid,” Sugiura apologized, “but you’re gonna have to listen to Kasuga on this one.”
“I promise, Chihiro and Haruto are both gonna be safe,” Kasuga assured him. “Trust me.”
“I want to fight by your side!” Taichi exclaimed. “Uncle Kaz wouldn’t have run from this fight, so
neither will I!”
“Kiryu wouldn’t have wanted you getting yourself killed either,” Zhao pointed out. “Let the
professionals handle this one.”
Kasuga nodded to Sugiura, who rolled up the window and turned the car around, driving away
from the scene.
“Turn around!” Taichi demanded. “Do you hear me? Turn around!”
“Not happening, kid.”
“Somebody that I love is in danger!” Taichi exclaimed. “Both of them! Haruto’s in danger, and
Chihiro’s in danger! What if they get killed when I could’ve stopped it?! Do you even know what

that’s like? I bet you don’t.”
Sugiura glared at Taichi in his mirror. “Don’t go there.”
As Sugiura drove away, with Taichi bitching in his ear about it the whole time, Kasuga, Adachi,
Zhao, and Joongi walked towards the Daidoji roadblock, with Kasuga twirling his bat as he
approached them. “Yo! Hanawa-san,” he greeted rather casually. “You brought out the welcome
wagon just for me? You shouldn’t have.”
Hanawa narrowed his eyes at Kasuga. “Your foolishness truly knows no bounds, Ichiban Kasuga.”
“Yeah, I get that a lot. Now, look, I really don’t wanna have to fight you,” Kasuga warned, “but
plans changed, and I’m gonna need to get by you. You understand, right?”
“Oh, I understand,” Hanawa growled. “I understand that you are a nuisance that I should have
taken care of a LONG time ago. Last chance, Kasuga. Turn around, and walk away.”
“Not a chance.”
“Then you’ve brought this upon yourself.” Hanawa nodded to his underlings and tossed his
cigarette on the ground. “Kill them,” he ordered as he turned around and started walking in the
direction of the orphanage.
Adachi groaned as the group got ready for a fight. “You know what? I’m gonna say it. Fuck. Every.
Single. One. Of these Daidoji Faction pricks.”

Taichi sat in the back of Sugiura’s car, arms crossed as they drove back to Naha. After he stopped
complaining, the car fell eerily silent, which made the entire ride that much more uncomfortable.
Sugiura sighed.
“Taichi,” he said, “you have nothing to worry about. Kasuga’s got this.”
“He shouldn’t have to do this alone,” Taichi reasoned. “I can help. The Daidoji might kill him!
They might kill Chihiro… and if they don’t, who knows what Chihiro will do with Haruto.”
“What, and you think you’re the solution to that problem?”
Taichi leaned forward. “Sugiura-san… What would you do in my place? The people you care about
are in danger, and you’re supposed to just sit back and trust that justice is coming, with or without
you."
Sugiura’s grip on the wheel tightened. “Kasuga’s got this.”
“Do you have family, Sugiura-san?”
Sugiura didn’t answer.
“I said—.”
“I heard you,” Sugiura cut him off.

“So answer me. Whatever. I guess you don’t. If you did, you’d know how I feel.”
“I understand what you’re going through,” Sugiura growled, “believe me, I do, but what do you
expect to—?”
“Anything!” Taichi exclaimed. “Anything at all. Because as much as I trust Kasuga… If something
happened to Haruto, or Chihiro, or ANYONE at Morning Glory…”
Images of Sugiura’s late sister flashed in his mind. Emi Terasawa. Her life cut short by a madman.
He couldn’t get the image out of his head.
Emi Terasawa. Her body, lying on the floor of her burning apartment, covered in her own blood. A
multitude of stab wounds covered her chest and stomach. Fear frozen in her eyes, forever. Her last
tears staining her cheeks.
Emi Terasawa. The woman whose death could’ve been prevented, if only…
“…if anything happened to them, and I wasn’t there to stop it,” Taichi continued, “I’d never forgive
myself. Especially since I’m entrusting their safety to somebody I barely know…”
Images of Takayuki Yagami in the courtroom flashed in Sugiura’s mind. It wasn’t his fault that Emi
died. It wasn’t. But, whether it was fair of not, a small part of Sugiura still held him responsible, as
the man who got her involved in his first murder case all those years ago. She’d still be alive today
if Yagami had just looked the other way when Shinpei Okubo was accused of murder at the ADDC.
But that wouldn’t have been right, either. He’d simply be trading one innocent life for another.
Here, however… did there need to be a trade?
“Sugiura-san… In a situation like that… if there was anything you could do to create a better
outcome, wouldn’t you do it?” Taichi asked.
Sugiura took a deep breath. “Yeah,” he answered. “Yeah. I would. Maybe there’s nothing I could’ve
done anyway. Maybe I couldn’t have changed anything at all. But I didn’t try. I just trusted that
justice would run its course… And you know what? That’s bullshit. If you can take justice into
your own hands, you gotta dole it out, no matter who tries to stop you!”
Taichi smiled and nodded. “Exactly! …Uh, wait, are we still talking about Haruto and Chihiro,
or…?”
Suddenly, Sugiura slammed on the brakes and whipped the car around, his tires screeching as he
did a complete 180, and started driving back towards Morning Glory. Taichi cheered him on as the
car sped towards its destination.

Kasuga and his allies stood before their defeated Daidoji foes. “Come on, guys,” he ordered.
“We’re almost there.”
“I’m sure there’s more Daidoji assholes where that came from,” Adachi said. “Keep your guard
up.”
The four of them ran up the road, inching closer to Morning Glory Orphanage, their progress
periodically impeded by more Daidoji Faction thugs who ultimately proved to be of little

consequence now that the party was better prepared to deal with them. “Kasuga-kun,” Zhao said
after one fighy. “What‘s the plan once we reach the orphanage?”
“Haven’t figured that part out yet,” Kasuga admitted. “If Chihiro isn’t there yet, probably, uh…
kidnap Haruto Sawamura?”
“So… exactly what she told Hanawa we were planning on doing,” Adachi said.
“Y-yeah. She kind of forced our hand on that one,” Kasuga admitted. “I’m thinking we’ll have to
take him back to Ijincho and just sort of lay low until his mom’s trial is over. Then we’ll hand him
back over.”
“Yeah, and meanwhile you’ve got the entire government gunning for your ass,” Adachi laughed.
“Not only that, but Kazuma Kiryu is sure to get wind of it, and he doesn’t seem like the type to
ignore something like that. Does this really sound like a good idea to you?”
“Look, I’m thinking as I go, give me a break, okay?”
“What if they find her guilty?” Joongi asked. “Haruka Sawamura, I mean.”
“Well, Hanawa said they’ve got a plant in the court,” Kasuga reasoned. “I don’t think we have to
worry about that.”
“And… what if Chihiro’s already snatched the kid?” Zhao asked.
“Then we figure out where she’s taking him and follow them. And hopefully find her before the
Daidoji do.”
“She did say something about taking the ‘asset’ to Osaka,” Zhao mused. “Probably a lot of boats
bound for Hong Kong out there, and Sotenbori’s got one of the largest triad populations in Japan
outside of Yokohama now that the Omi Alliance is gone.”
Kasuga hummed. “Hmm. Sotenbori, eh? Isn’t that where Sugiura-san said his detective buddy’s
laying low? That means we’ve already got contacts there. Plus, the old Tojo Clan guard is there too,
Daigo Dojima and the others, and the Omi Alliance captain too, but… I’m not even sure how to get
in touch with them.” He sighed. “I wonder what Mabuchi has on Chihiro, though.”
“Maybe nothing,” Zhao said. “Maybe she’s on board 100%.”
“Nah, that can’t be true,” Kasuga denied. “I saw the way she looked at Taichi. That was real. No
way she’d do this if she wasn’t being forced to. Something else is going on here.”
Adachi wasn’t convinced. “She works for Japan’s most top-secret government organization.
Mabuchi shouldn’t even be able to touch her. Face it, Kasuga… She's a traitor. Straight-up.”
“Agh, that can’t be true, though…” Kasuga groaned. “Ah… dammit. Poor Taichi. Not even twenty
four hours, and his first love has already broken his heart.”
“That’s… a melodramatic way of putting it,” Adachi chuckled.
Finally, they could see the orphanage. All the lights were out. Everyone must’ve been asleep. That
was good. That meant they had beaten Chihiro here. Unfortunately, it also meant that, as far as the

Daidoji were concerned, they were still the enemy, so when Hanawa stepped in front of them as
they approached the orphanage, they didn’t expect a friendly chat.
“You’re really starting to piss me off, Kasuga,” he growled. “I know you think you’re doing
something heroic here, but you’re actually just making an ass of yourself.”
“Hanawa-san, we’re on the same side,” Kasuga pled. “You gotta believe us. We just want what’s
best for the kid.”
“I’m sure you do,” Hanawa replied. “I don’t doubt that. But it’s really not any of your business. The
Daidoji have been operating right here, underneath the orphans’ noses, for the better part of six
years, and you’re screwing all of that up!”
“We just wanna take Haruto away from where the Saio Triad are operating until Haruka gets out of
jail,” Kasuga claimed. “Wouldn’t you rather be safe than sorry?”
“I would rather you get over yourself!” Hanawa exclaimed as he pulled out an electrified baton,
which crackled with energy. “This ends right here, right now, Ichiban Kasuga!” He ran at the group
with his baton in the air and swung at Kasuga, who dodged the attack. He then swung at Adachi,
who deflected the attack with his own baton, and ducked just in time to miss a slash from Zhao’s
broadsword. He rolled away from the group, then charged at Kasuga and swung once again.
Kasuga pulled his bat out and blocked the attack, their glaring faces illuminated in the darkness by
the baton’s sparks.
KIHEI HANAWA
Daidoji Faction
Hanawa jumped backwards and held a defensive stance. “You’re really starting to get on my
nerves, Kasuga!” he called out.
“Yeah? Well up yours too, buddy,” Kasuga replied. He ran at Hanawa with a tenacious fist raised,
winding up an attack and swinging, as he punched him in the face and sent him backwards.
Hanawa was quick to get back on his feet and activated his rocket shoes, allowing him to move
twice per turn. He then grabbed one end of his baton. He split the baton in half and held one half in
each hand. He swung the two batons, causing the glowing blue cables from their first fight to fly
out and grab Joongi and Zhao, immobilizing them.
“Agh! Sorry, guys…” Zhao apologized as he found the bindings too strong to overcome. Joongi
was similarly in a tough spot.
“I’m up!” Adachi yelled as his turn came around. He ran up to Hanawa and grabbed him by his
legs and swung him around, then let go, causing him to fly across the yard. Undeterred, Hanawa
stood back up and attacked Kasuga, swinging his baton at him. Kasuga rolled backwards to dodge
the attack, not that it did much good as Hanawa’s speed meant he could just attack again. The
second attack connected, shocking Kasuga, but thankfully not paralyzing him. In response, Kasuga
backed up, then, dragging his bat along the floor, he ran at Hanawa. Once he reached him, he
swung the bat upwards and jumped into the air, sending Hanawa into the air with him, and then
swung his bat downwards, sending Hanawa crashing into the ground.
“Tch!” Hanawa scoffed as he stood up. “You’re persistent this time around. Fine. Let’s see how you
handle this!” He tapped an icon on his smartwatch and three small drones arrived to back him up.

“You know something? These weren’t even that expensive. We bought these off of the Seiryo High
Robotics Club.”
“A… high school robotics club?” Kasuga asked. “Seriously? The government can’t shell out for
something a little more… professional?”
“These students were particularly gifted,” Hanawa responded, smirking. “Observe.” He issued a
command to the drones. It was at this point that Kasuga noticed that each of the three drones had a
small projectile cannon on their undersides. The first targeted Adachi, rapidly firing a series of
small electrified projectiles which gave him a series of painful shocks.
“Ngh! Oh, that’s not good,” he groaned as he fell to the ground, stunned. The next drone fired a
shotgun blast, spread across a large area, at Zhao and Joongi, similarly shocking them. The third
one simply trained its sights on Kasuga and emitted a red laser, which stayed trained on him no
matter where he went.
“What the hell…? What kinda hardware were these high schoolers working with?!” Kasuga asked.
“Their outside counselor was very resourceful,” Hanawa chuckled.
“Kasuga,” Adachi said as he stood up. “If we want any chance at beating this guy, we gotta take his

Joongi agreed. “Starting with the one that hasn’t fired yet. I have a feeling that once it does, you’re
in for a world of pain.”
Kasuga nodded. “Right.” He imagined a translucent protective barrier surrounding Hanawa which
wouldn’t go away until the drones were destroyed. Realizing he could probably destroy two of

two drones to Hanawa’s left; the machine gunner was destroyed, but the shotgunner still had some

“I got you, Kasuga!” Zhao called out as his paralysis wore off. He ran at the sniper drone, which

With all three drones down, Adachi was able to move on Hanawa. He did have a pair of handcuffs
on him; maybe he could just cuff him and be done with it? He tried just that, but Hanawa, of
course, was too fast for him and dodged the attack; and even if Adachi had cuffed him, he probably
could’ve easily gotten free of the cuffs. They were dealing with a government agent after all, sort

“Is that the best you can do?” Hanawa taunted. He pulled out a pack of his explosive cigarettes, but
instead of pulling one out and lighting it, held the lighter to the package. Once it was aflame, he
tossed the package into the air, sending all twenty of the cigarettes inside flying and essentially
carpet bombing the area with explosives, damaging everyone on the field. He then ran at Adachi
with his baton and cracked him across the head with it, knocking him out. “Gee, this seems
familiar,” Hanawa chuckled. “Who’s next?”

Zhao growled at Hanawa and dashed towards him, broadsword drawn. Hanawa caught the attack
with ease, using his baton to block the sword’s downward swing, and then electrifying the blade,

“Guys!” Kasuga called out. “Ngh…”
Hanawa returned his attention to Kasuga and stepped towards him, menacingly. “This brings me no

“Stop!” a deep voice commanded from the shadows. Everyone looked over at the source of the

“Ah, yes… Kasuga… That does ring a bell.”

“Heh. Perhaps.”

Kasuga was confused. “H-huh?”

“Aw, come on, man, this is getting old…” Kasuga groaned. “Look. You guys have a traitor in the

Chapter 26: For Your Sake

“I see… so that’s why you can’t see your kids,” Kasuga said, having had basically Kiryu’s entire
backstory since his supposed death in 2016 explained to him while the two men walked along the

“I know,” Kiryu sighed as he lit a cigarette.
“And, with the Tojo and Omi gone, most of the organized crime threats against them are pretty
much gone too.”
“I know,” Kiryu repeated.
“So… why are you still working for these Daidoji assholes, then?” Kasuga asked. “The CLP
doesn’t even control the government anymore. Surely you could’ve gotten out a while ago.”
“You’re probably right,” Kiryu conceded. “But… I made a deal with them. I’m going to uphold my
end of the deal until they cut me loose voluntarily.”
“You do know they aren’t gonna do that, right?”
Kiryu nodded. “Yeah. But I still have no intention of running from my responsibilities to the
Daidoji.”
“Well, I guess that makes you a better man than me,” Kasuga chuckled. “If it were me, I’d have cut

“Is that so?” Kiryu asked, smirking. “Strange. Your loyalty to Masumi Arakawa after eighteen
years in prison without so much as a visit painted a strikingly different picture.”
“Ah… Okay, yeah, you got me there. But, still though. Arakawa-san was like family to me… He
wasn’t like family, he WAS family. The Daidoji are just your employers. That’s different, right?”
Kiryu sighed and thought about his next words for a moment. He decided to answer his question
with a slight change of subject. “Do you know what Haruka’s been up to in the last few days?”
“Huh?”
“She’s been through a lot, just this week alone, with some of your… ‘party’, you call them, yes? Yu
Nanba, Seonhee… and Saeko Mukoda.”

“Uh…”
“And yes, she’s in a bad spot right now. But… She’s grown into such a strong young woman. Not
just physically. Emotionally. She’s strong-willed, and has an even stronger sense of justice than I

Kiryu took a drag from his cigarette as he stared out at the ocean, the waves lighting up in the
moonlight. “She’s always been strong. When she was nine years old, she went through so much,

“I thought, and I still think, that she had the strength to push forward without me even then. She
just didn’t realize that. When I faked my death, she had to find that strength within her, and I’m
afraid that, if she were to realize I was always around, watching her from the shadows, that she’ll
lose it all over again. The same goes for everyone else. I’ve been watching them grow up afar, and
in doing so, I realized… They don’t need me anymore. Nobody does.”
Kasuga was silent after hearing that. He thought long and hard about the things he wanted to say
and the best, most tactful, most delicate way to say those things. Finally, he found the words.
“Kiryu-san… Do you even fuckin’ hear yourself right now?!”
“What?” Kiryu replied, flatly.
“That is, without a doubt, the dumbest fucking thing I have ever heard,” Kasuga said, rather

I’m one of those morons, and I don’t think I’ve ever said anything that dumb.”
Kiryu narrowed his eyes at Kasuga. “Do you disagree? You’ve been hanging around Taichi. Can
you honestly say he needs me?”
Kasuga laughed. “Dude, who cares if anyone needs you,” he replied. “Is that the only thing that

“I don’t follow.”
“Agh, look, man, what I’m trying to say is… Who cares what you think they need. What do you

Kiryu was confused. “What do I… want?”
“Have you seriously never asked yourself that before?” Kasuga asked. “Come on, man, you’ve

Kiryu was slightly offended. “54…”
“And you said you joined the Daidoji six years ago, after leaving prison, right? And before that,

“My point is, if you don’t think you have to live for others anymore, then live for yourself,

“I…” Kiryu thought about his words. Live for myself? What could he mean by that? He shook his

It was a chilly and crowded December evening in Osaka’s Sōtenbori district. The air was slightly
colder than was normal for this part of Japan, but this didn’t do much to discourage the nightlife.
Droves of people crowded all up and down the district, coming and going from the various shops,
restaurants, bars, and cabaret clubs that lined the streets. Still more people arrived by the minute
from elsewhere in Osaka; business was booming.
Not all were here for pleasure, however, as Kazuma Kiryu pushed his way to the front of a crowd
that had gathered before a large television screen that sat atop a building across from the Cabaret
Grand, watching coverage of a breaking news story from out of Tokyo.
“…Tokyo Metropolitan Police are in shock today, following a series of events which led to the
escape of a large number of inmates from all throughout the Kanto region, and the prison itself in a
state of extreme disrepair. Among the most notable escapees were suspected members of the Tojo
Clan’s successor organization, the Shin Tojo Alliance.” Kiryu gasped as an image of Haruka came
onscreen. “Suspected Chairwoman Haruka Sawamura is at-large and wanted by police.”
“What the hell is going on…?” Kiryu muttered under his breath. The Saio Triad, the Seiryu Clan,
this fixation that the Tokyo Police had on Haruka… he needed to get to the bottom of it, and fast.
He pressed a finger to an earpiece he wore as he pushed his way back through the crowd to get to
the street. “Kasuga, are you at the location yet?”

OMI ALLIANCE

Kiryu and Taichi approached the old Omi Alliance headquarters. As he expected, the place was

Yagami made his way back into Sotenbori and sat in the corner of a Smile Burger that he had sort
of adopted as his base of operations, in the sense that he kept coming back here and nobody had
kicked him out yet despite the fact that he only ever ordered a small soda. He crossed his arms as
he poured over the details of the case, and his face wrinkled in frustration as he realized he was still
no closer to figuring out just what the hell was going on.
Haruka Sawamura was arrested for murdering the Seiryu Clan’s captain. This happened on the
same day she asked Kaito to investigate the Daidoji Faction. At the same time, despite not being
anywhere near the murder scene, myself, Higashi, Sugiura, and Tsukumo were all implicated as coconspirators, as was Ichiban Kasuga, a former Tojo Clan grunt who just served his own stint in
prison for a similar crime. Before taking the bar exam, Yagami recalled researching the Ichiban
Kasuga murder case. It flew a little under the radar, being that it seemed to be a classic and
unsurprising case of yakuza-on-yakuza violence, but as he looked into the details of the case, he
realized that almost nothing about it made any sense, just as Haruka Sawamura’s supposed murder
of a yakuza boss itself makes very little sense.
But he knew from experience that sometimes, the police weren’t interested in justice, and the
Tokyo PD in particular has made more than one arrest in the past for the sake of closing a case
rather than to see justice done. All one had to do to verify this was ask Shinpei Okubo, who was
wrongly accused of two murders, or Akihiro Ehara, who nearly got away with one he did commit,
in both cases because prosecutors in Tokyo drew their conclusions before all of the evidence was
available to them.

Chihiro’s finger wrapped around the trigger. She started to pull it… but did not complete the action.

A deafening gunshot rang out, a blinding flare engulfed the muzzle, and a bullet shot through the
homeless leader’s head, killing him instantly. His body fell to the floor, his extremities briefly
convulsing before going limp. A pool of blood formed underneath the exit wound. The homeless
nearby panicked and started to rush for the exits.
“No!” Chihiro wailed as she dropped the gun in shock at what she had just done. She fell to her

violently. She felt like she was going to vomit. Feeling something wet on her nose, she instinctively
wiped it off and glanced at her palm.
It was blood.
His blood.
She had just killed a man. A man who trusted her.
Murderer. The word rang in her head repeatedly, taunting her. She started to hyperventilate as the
realization set in. Murderer. Her heartbeat was so loud in her own ears that she almost didn’t hear
her master’s cruel laughter from her side. She slowly looked up at him. “Wh… why?” she asked in
barely a whisper, unable to speak any louder.
He simply smirked. “Hmph. Don’t worry,” he said, his smirk slowly growing into a grin. “It gets

If she had any doubts about what she was doing, they were gone now. She was in too deep. Slowly,

Haruka quickly pivoted on her toe and stood up, then tossed her head slightly back to get her hair

With Kaito and Higashi focused on the randos swarming the party, Haruka, Saeko, Nanba, and
Seonhee were able to focus on Fake Kiryu. “Say… did Kiryu-san ever need goons?” Saeko asked.
“Nope,” Haruka replied flatly. “He’s a one-man army. What would he need goons for?”
“For real… Guy laid an ass-whooping on all seven of us by himself last time,” Nanba said, wincing

“…Hunk?” Haruka asked with a tilt of her head, confused and a little disturbed. She shook the
thought away and made the first move, running at Fake Kiryu and hitting him with a right low kick,
a mid left kick, and a double roundhouse kick, which knocked him down. He quickly stood up and
tried to grab Haruka. She was agile enough to roll backwards and dodge it, resulting in a miss and
the end of his turn.
Saeko was up next. She pulled out a bottle of champagne and shook it, popping the top off and
beaning him in the forehead, dealing a surprising amount of damage; the resulting spray of alcohol
drenched him, and he found himself dealing with a cold. She then chucked the empty bottle at his
face, doing even more damage.
Nanba chugged his own bottle of liquor and held a lighter in front of his face, igniting the alcohol
in his breath and spewing the flames out at Fake Kiryu, igniting his clothing. “Ah! Hot! Hot!” he
cried out as he patted his clothes to put the fire out.
At the start of her turn, Seonhee jumped at him, legs first, and gripped his sides with her thighs,
then twisted her legs to send him to the ground. She let go of him at terminal velocity and landed
gracefully on her feet, while Fake Kiryu hit the ground, hard. He groaned in pain as he stood up.
With her turn coming back around, Haruka decided to make use of a tool she’d received at the start
of her journey. She pulled her phone out and tapped the Poundmates app, which seemed to have
gained a lot of new users since she last used it. Frantically, she navigated the app’s menus, looking
for a new profile. She swiped and tapped faster and faster, static electricity sparking from her finger
as she did so, before she finally found the icon of a tough-looking ally… and somebody that Kaito
mentioned to her earlier.
“Please…” she said as she tapped the icon, then held the phone up to the sky. “I NEED YOUR
HELP!” she shouted to the heavens. A beam of light emanated from her phone and shot into the
sky above.
A new ally jumped into action, landing on the battlefield between Haruka and her opponent. He
was a middle-aged man with short black hair and a thin goatee, wearing a brown leather jacket,
black jeans, and a pair of dark brown leather combat boots. “Who’s the bully you want me to take
care of?” he asked as he turned to face Fake Kiryu.
JIN KUWANA
Handyman of Ijincho
“I’ll show you true suffering!” Kuwana yelled out. He threw a right cross, a left back fist, and a

door. “Your actions have consequences,” he said in a low growl. “A pity you didn’t realize… until
it was too late.” He then stepped out of the freezer and shut the door, trapping Fake Kiryu.

As with before, Haruka came out of the fantasy having done a great deal of damage to her enemy,

“Okay… Never mind…” Fake Kiryu made his move, running at Haruka and drop kicking her in the

its place.
She laid on the ground, barely able to move as her heartbeat slowed… It felt like it was only
beating once per second, driven by an imaginary countdown to zero. “Damn it…” she muttered to
herself as she waited for death to consume her. She had come so far, only to be defeated by a faker
usurping her father’s name. Was this really how her story ended?
No… it couldn’t be. This wasn’t how things were supposed to go. Slowly, her fingers twitched. Her
pulse started to quicken. Her eyes shot open, and she glared up at the arena’s ceiling. “No… I won’t
be stopped here!” she exclaimed dramatically as she stood up, rejuvenated. She was bruised, but
she refused to be beaten.
Nanba rolled his eyes. “Drama queen,” he muttered.
“Haven’t had enough?” the imposter chuckled as his red heat aura reappeared, signaling to Haruka
that his attacks would still be of increased power going forward. “It doesn’t matter. I’ll finish you

It was Saeko’s turn again. “Hope you’re ready!” she growled at her opponent as she approached

On her turn, Seonhee pulled a crossbow out—where she got it, Haruka wasn’t sure—and shot Fake
Kiryu in the face. “I’m… so glad you’re on my side…” Haruka muttered.
“Most people would be,” Seonhee said, smirking.
After Nanba spread birdseed over the arena and directed a flock of pigeons to attack, it was

could, sending him tumbling to the ground so hard that he actually bounced off of it. It did a lot of

damage, but it wasn’t enough, and he stood back up a moment later. She figured that maybe one

Kaito punched the last of Fake Kiryu’s goons into unconsciousness, and he and Higashi rejoined

“Uh… like in what, now?”
Haruka gained a new ability right then and there, and she would be remiss not to use it. Any time a
group of enemies—or, in the case, the last remaining enemy—was knocked down, be it from
