“Let’s get this party started!” the announcer exclaimed as the fight began. Sugiura was enveloped
by a white flash of light, as was Haruka, and they both took their battle stances.
FUMIYA SUGIURA
Yokohama 99
Haruka was by herself for the first time since her journey began, but she refused to be intimidated.
If it was a fight this Sugiura guy wanted, it was a fight he was going to get. She made the first
move, approaching him and throwing a basic rush combo at him consisting of a right low kick, a
mid left kick, and a double roundhouse kick.
Sugiura simply shrugged the attacks off as his turn came around. He pulled a Red Bull energy drink
out of his pocket, lifted his mask, and chugged the drink, then crushed the can and threw it away
before slotting his mask back onto his face. “Oh yeah, I’m really feeling it now!” he exclaimed.
The caffeine, taurine, and B vitamins pumped him up, allowing him to move twice a turn. He used
his next move to hit Haruka with a lightning fast combo consisting of a hopping right high inward
crescent kick, a right rising kick, and a 180 degree somersault kick.
Haruka’s turn was up. She hit him with a backflip double kick, knocking him down. She then used
this opportunity to make an extra attack, and kicked him across the floor.
Sugiura’s next turn began with him standing up and running at Haruka. He shoved her, dealing no
damage, and Haruka wondered what the point of the attack was… until she felt her pockets and
noticed that they were a bit lighter. “Huh?” she gasped. Chuckling, Sugiura held up her phone.
“Lose something?” he taunted as he pocketed her phone, leaving her unable to call for help using
Poundmates for the duration of the fight. He used his second move to hit her with a spinning right
heel kick and a hand standing roundhouse kick.

“Ah!” she grunted as she stumbled backwards. None of his attacks were hitting particularly hard,
though. “You’re holding back,” she observed.
“Honestly, I’m just trying to win,” Sugiura chuckled. “It’d be a bit fucked up if I went all out here.”
“Well you better start.”
“Huh?”
“You’re making a mistake by underestimating me, Sugiura-san,” Haruka warned. She went on the
offensive, running at him and jumping into the air, hoping to hit him with a running kick. Sugiura
dodged the attack and caused Haruka to kick the wall instead; what he didn’t anticipate, however,
was that Haruka would kick herself off of the wall itself and use this as the jumpoff for another
attack, backflipping towards Sugiura and hitting him with a double downward kick.
“Yeah, come on, Haruka!” Kaito cheered from the back of the cage. “Beat his ass!”
“Isn’t that your friend?” Saeko asked, an eyebrow raised.
“Ah, friends need to be humbled, sometimes,” Kaito chuckled. “I’ve kicked Tak’s ass a few times,
Tak has kicked my ass, we’ve both kicked Higashi’s ass. What’s an ass-kicking among friends?”
Smirking, he leaned in, and his tone dropped to an almost conspiratorial whisper. “Say… you’ve
still got shit you need to settle with Ichiban Kasuga, right? Next time we see him… let’s kick his
ass!”
“I’m good, thanks… Hmm… Actually…”
Haruka’s attention was turned from her party’s conversation back to Sugiura when he taunted her
with a rather obnoxious dance he’d seen on the internet. “Come get me!” he called out.
She knew, however, that he was trying to throw her off, and refused to allow herself to be enraged
by his display of jackassery. “…That’s not funny,” she muttered. Miss!
Sugiura used his second turn to run at her and reverse roundhouse kick her. She was able to guard
against the attack, halving the damage the attack would have done, and retaliated with a knockback
technique that she had seen Kiryu use, dealing a small amount of damage to Sugiura. His Red Bull
wore off that turn, and he returned to only being able to move once a turn. “Ah, man… I think I’m

“I’m up!” Haruka exclaimed as her turn came back around. She got on the floor, swept his ankles
with her own, causing his feet to leave the ground, then quickly jumped up and kicked his face,

making each move, she could have followed up with further attacks to juggle Sugiura, but alas, she

Sugiura regained his footing and attacked with a right push kick and a left roundhouse kick. Haruka
retaliated with a roundhouse kick of her own, which connected a little too hard with his face and

“Give up, yet?” Haruka asked.

EX-OMI ALLIANCE GOONS
Adachi, Joongi, and Zhao stood up against several ex-Omi Alliance goons. Their fight took place

Saeko smiled softly. “Give him hell, Haruka.”

Haruka nodded. “Yeah. Sugiura-san… It’s time to end this fight.” She was having a revelation. By
expending all of her energy, she’d be able to move as fast as Kiryu could have, and for a short time
break the conventions of the almost turn-based style in which she’d been fighting thus far. This
state wouldn’t last long… but she didn’t need long. She signaled this change by roundhouse
kicking the air, and everyone around her seemed to freeze as she moved like a dragon.
She ran up to him and hit him faster than he could react. She first hit him with a series of left and
right hooks, then roundhouse kicked his face with such intensity that time seemed to slow down;
she followed this up with a sideways push kick of similar intensity; Sugiura fell over, and Haruka
finished the job with a heavy stomp into his chest, taking all of his breath away. The battle lost, he
stared up at her in shock. She simply smiled at him as the crowd cheered, although it was quite
clear that she was out of breath, practically panting from the over exertion.
“HA-RU-KA! HA-RU-KA! HA-RU-KA!”
Adachi finished beating down the last of his group’s enemies and looked into the cage, gasping.

The chants continued, and Haruka let out a breathless chuckle. “Hah… I… I told you not to

Haruka and her party stood at a rather unassuming grave in an unimportant spot in the sprawling

her arms crossed. “I know how ya feel, Haruka-chan… Seems we both have a lot to learn about
love.”
He made his way down the street level, grabbed his jacket, and again followed her, this time east
onto South Shofukucho, and then north onto East Shofukucho, passing Kiryu—still wearing his
Ono Michio costume and in the midst of entertaining children—on the way. He watched Haruka
pass, then watched Kasuga pass.
“Heh… Yo, Ono Michio-kun. Having fun?”
“Nice to michi,” Kiryu said flatly, his voice muffled by the mask. “Have a michi Christmas…”
What the fuck does that even mean?
Kasuga laughed, then continued following Haruka, who turned right into Ashitaba Park, though he
could still hear Kiryu on the next street over attempting to spread Christmas cheer. “Ho ho ho,
michi! Have you been good for Santa Michio? …ugh…”
Haruka made her way to a bench in the park and sat down, sighing. “What the hell is wrong with
me…?” she asked herself, before yelling out in frustration. “Agh! Why did I do that? Why did I
kiss her?! Idiot!” As she berated herself, Kasuga caught up, but stayed hidden around the corner to
listen in on her thoughts. “She loves Kasuga, you already knew that, dumbass! What, did you think
she was going to drop everything, drop her job, drop her friends, drop the man who got there way
before you, and come back to Okinawa with you?”
“Hm…” Kasuga hummed as he listened in. Just hearing this was giving him a bit of an epiphany.
“Just because I got there first doesn’t mean I’m the best choice… I gotta work for it, same as you.”
“And what about Yuta?! He’s been dead less than two years and, what, now I’m trying to replace
him? Oh, I’m terrible! I’m such a terrible woman!”
“Okay, she’s tortured herself enough over this,” Kasuga chuckled. He stepped out to introduce
himself, when a group of men in suits surrounded Haruka. “Hm?”
“Well, look who it is,” the leader laughed, leering at Haruka. “Remember us?”
“Huh? No…” Haruka tried to think back as to who these men could be. “Uh… wait… You were the
men I met my first time here, right?”
“Oh! She does remember!” The man laughed, as did his buddies. “Yeah. That’s us. You treated us
so rudely. And then, yer loan shark buddy came over and beat the shit out of us!”
“You sort of deserved it…” Haruka muttered, before shaking her head and standing up. “Whatever.
I don’t have time for this.”
“You’re gonna make time, bitch!” the man yelled threateningly. “I can’t help but notice that yer
loan shark friend ain’t here right now! It’s also not lost on us that you are a wanted criminal.
Now… if ya treat us real nice… we might not go to the cops. If not… we’re gonna take what we’re
owed.”

“Like hell you are,” Kasuga said in a low growl as he stepped around the corner. Confused, Haruka
turned to him.
“Who…?”
The man accosting Haruka raised an eyebrow. “Huh? And who the fuck are you?”
“Oh, nobody… Just an ordinary guy who really doesn’t like your tone.” He took off his sunglasses
and threw his cap down, allowing them to see the angered look in his eyes. “Back off, fellas. Before
this gets ugly.” The leader scoffed and spat on Kasuga, clearly not having learned his lesson from
the last two beatings dished out to him and his crew. “Hey!” Kasuga exclaimed, stepping back.
“Fuck off, you yakuza-lookin’ motherfucker. We’ll kill you, too!”
“Hmph… Alright, can’t say I didn’t try,” Kasuga chuckled as he pulled out his bat.
“I don’t know who you are,” Haruka muttered, “but I can take care of myself.”
“Oh, I believe you. But I’ve never been able to turn down a good ass-kicking. Believe me, this is
just for sport.” With a laugh, he twirled his bat in the air and pointed it at his opponents like a
sword. “THE BATTLE IS ON!”
ASSHOLES
The three men were enveloped in white flashes of light as they transformed, much to Haruka’s
chagrin. “Tch… When are they going to stop transforming?” she asked herself.
“Huh? No way, you see it too?!” Kasuga exclaimed.
“Hm? Wait… you can see the monsters?”
“Hell yeah! It’s way more fun when they go all RPG monster on ya!”
“Just who are you?”
Kasuga smirked. “The name’s Kasuga.”
“…! Kasuga…?!”
“I can tell you all about myself in a minute. But first, these assholes need to be dealt with.” He
moved first, twirling his bat in the air and swinging it hard at one of the man’s lackeys. None of
them were particularly strong, so this one hit was enough to take him down. “Aw, man. And here I
thought this fight would be fun.”
“Let’s do this!” Haruka exclaimed as her turn came up. She performed a leg sweep on the other
lackey, sending him to the air, then rolled backwards and kicked her feet out, jumping into the air
and hitting him in midair. She landed the resulting backflip perfectly, while he landed face-first on
the ground, knocked out.
The leader slashed at Kasuga with his knife, though this did pitiful damage, and Kasuga responded
in kind by backing up and running at him with his bat dragging along the ground. He jumped into
the air and raised his bat, sending the leader into the air. He landed on the ground, unable to fight,
ending this very pathetic fight with minimal effort.

Haruka relaxed as she stared at the three men, groaning from their injuries. They stood up and very
quickly made their exit. “Come on, let’s get out of here!” the leader exclaimed in fear as he ran
away, his two friends following close behind.
“Huh, I thought that would be harder,” Kasuga chuckled. “You alright, Haruka-chan?”
“You’re… Ichiban Kasuga…?”
“I, uh, take it you’ve heard of me?” Kasuga asked. He didn’t want to give away that he saw what
happened between her and Saeko, so he played dumb for the time being. “Thing is… I’ve been
lookin’ for you, Haruka Sawamura.”
“Were you the one who was following me earlier?”
Kasuga frowned. “Y-yeah. Sorry, didn’t mean to creep you out. It’s just… I heard you were in a bit
of a bind, and…” Suddenly, Haruka fell to her knees, alarming Kasuga. “Huh? What’s wrong? Are
you hurt?! Oh, shit, did they get you?!” Kiryu-san’s gonna be pissed! “Don’t worry, I’ll get help!
Just stay there, and…”
“You saw everything, didn’t you?”
“I… huh?”
“With Saeko… Kasuga-san…” Haruka placed her hands in front of her and assumed a dogeza
position, placing her forehead on the ground. She started to cry. “I’m sorry, Kasuga!”
“Whoa, hey, hold on, what are you even sorry for? ‘Cause you kissed someone you like? That’s not
a crime.”
“I know about you and Saeko…” she explained. “I knew it when I kissed her. I knew what I was
doing was wrong, and I did it anyway! I’m so, so sorry! I don’t know why I did it, I just… it just
happened! You must think I’m horrible! I…”
“Haruka.” Haruka flinched upon hearing her name. “Look at me.” Slowly, Haruka sighed,
swallowed her shame, and sat up. She found herself struggling to actually meet Kasuga’s eyes. In
front of her, however, was an outstretched hand.
“H… huh?” Slowly, she looked up at his face. There was no anger in his eyes. All she saw was a
warm smile, as if he were greeting an old friend. The harsh light of the lamp post behind him
created an almost halo-like effect as it wrapped around his messy rat’s nest of a haircut.
“You’re not horrible. Don’t even think like that, because it ain’t true. Look… I’m not gonna
pretend that what I saw didn’t hurt,” he said. “Actually, it sort of felt like I was being stabbed in the
heart by a serrated knife dipped in salt. But trust me… I’ve felt way greater pains. This is nothing.
And I’m not gonna let it get in the way of my mission.”
“Your mission?”
“Heh. Yeah. Helping you,” he said with a chuckle. “The thing is… The whole situation with
Haruto… it’s my fault. I was at Morning Glory when he was taken, and I failed to keep him safe.
So really, it’s me who should be apologizing.” He clenched his fist and held it in front of his chest,

grinning at her. “But I’m going to set things right. That… is my promise to you, Haruka Sawamura.
And when I make a promise, I follow through. That’s the Ichiban Kasuga way.”
Slowly, Haruka stood up. “Y… you’re not mad?”
“Nah. I ain’t got nothing to be mad about,” he laughed, waving her concerns away. “I mean… It’s
not like she belongs to me. We’re not even dating. Not at the moment, anyway.”
“At the moment?”
Kasuga’s smile turned into a smirk. “Yeah. I’m not mad… but I’m also not giving up. Sa-chan
deserves only the best, wouldn’t you agree?”
“Of course.”
“So that means… I can’t wave the white flag. I’m gonna fight even harder to prove that I’m the guy
for her. And Haruka…” His grin returned. “I want you to fight just as hard! Because if I beat you
when you’re not even really trying, then I’m not really the best one for her. I’m just the only one
left.”
Haruka’s sadness was replaced by utter confusion. Kasuga’s entire attitude was puzzling. Suddenly,
a sound she thought she wouldn’t be able to produce again left her mouth—a laugh. “Heh. Hehe.
Hahahaha!” She started cracking up, with a laugh infectious enough to get Kasuga going too.
“Kasuga… they were right. You really are strange.”
“Heh… so whaddya say?” He held his hand out again. “Will you let me join the team, and set
everything right?”
Haruka’s smile faded. Her mirthful look was replaced with a determined one, and she grabbed
Kasuga’s hand and shook it. “Of course. I need all of the help I can get.”
“Then set your mind at ease… because help has arrived!” Kasuga exclaimed.
***
Saeko walked the streets of Sotenbori, thoroughly shaken. “What the shit was that?!” she
exclaimed, internally freaking out. “Was that some kind of joke? I don’t get it. Why would she…
Haruka doesn’t… does she?” She turned into an alleyway, pulled a pack of cigarettes and a lighter
out of her handbag, and quickly lit what turned out to be the last cigarette on her person. She
inhaled sharply, then blew out a puff of smoke as she tried to calm down. “Hm… But… I didn’t
handle that very well, did I? I just… freaked out and ran off again. Hmph. First Ichiban, and now
her… some friend you are…”
Truthfully, however, she had no idea how, if at all, she would address the situation with either of
them.

Chapter 51: Ono Michio: The Next Generation!
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

The Millennium Tower’s top floor was quiet on this chilly December evening. It often was, as over
the last two decades, tragedy after tragedy seems to have struck this set of offices, frightening away
prospective tenants. Indeed, by this point, some were beginning to wonder if the entire building
was cursed; local urban legends said that a property speculator, killed during a war between rival
yakuza families, was buried in an empty lot that sat in the center of the dilapidated shopping plaza
that the tower’s foundation was built over. Some believed that his ghost now haunted the complex,
and that every tragedy to strike was his doing.
Akio Yamamoto, however, was not a superstitious man. He sought to defy local legend, just as he
had defied every expectation society had set out for him, and now that he was on his way to the top,
he thought it only fitting to place his new office, which came with his new promotion, at the top,
overlooking all of the rats on the ground in Kamurocho.
So there he stood, at the very top, clad in his brand new white suit, black dress shirt, and white tie,
staring out of the window, looking down on society. Any man would be happy to have reached the
heights he reached.
But he was not happy, for the news was not good. The intercom sitting on his desk buzzed.
“Commissioner Yamamoto, Mafuyu Fujii with the Public Prosecutor’s Office is here to speak with
you.”
He turned to glare at the intercom device, before approaching it and pressing a button to page
through to his secretary. “Send her in,” he growled. A moment later, the woman herself, 36 years
old but with a face appearing much younger, entered.
“Yamamoto-san,” she greeted with a bow. “You wished to speak with me?” She had shoulderlength brown hair with a center part and wore a white pinstriped blazer with a matching skirt, as
well as a black undershirt and black heels. A pin denoting her status—Chief Prosecutor, newly
promoted—sat upon her lapel. That was something she had in common with Yamamoto; her recent
successes had put her on an elevator to the very top.
That was where the commonalities ended, however. “Yes,” Yamamoto said, maintaining a
professional air but with an undertone of contempt for the woman. “This morning, without
consulting the police department, your office dropped criminal charges against several individuals
connected with the Sawamura case. Why?”
“Yes, we’ve had to narrow the scope of our investigation,” she explained. “Forensic evidence has
failed to place anyone aside from Haruka Sawamura and Masaharu Kaito at the scene of the
murder, and even circumstantial evidence has failed to implicate many of those we were pursuing.”
“Even Ichiban Kasuga, the ex-yakuza with a second-degree murder on his rap sheet?” Yamamoto
questioned. “Do you understand how stupid you’re making your office look?”
“I visited his place of work in Yokohama and conducted interviews with his coworkers and
superiors,” Mafuyu replied. “He’d been on vacation for about three weeks prior to the murder, and

two and a half weeks prior to Haruka Sawamura’s arrival in Ijincho, according to the latter’s
railcard. What’s more, her cell phone records failed to establish any sort of link. We simply saw no
reason to continue investigating his involvement. If we had brought him to trial, it would have
almost certainly resulted in a failure to convict… and considering the embarrassment our office
faced after the retrial of Akihiro Ehara, we felt those kinds of mistakes would be best avoided
where we can spot them.”
“It’s all politics with you,” Yamamoto scoffed as he turned back to the window. “Fools. All of
you.”
“To be perfectly honest… The entire case is on the verge of falling apart.”
Yamamoto’s eyes widened. “Excuse me?”
“Jo Sawashiro visited our office today,” Mafuyu announced. “He’s now refusing to testify. What’s
more, he told us that there was a hard disk failure in the Seiryu Clan’s security office. All of the
footage of Sawamura and her associates illegally entering the compound… it’s gone.”
“That’s absurd!” Yamamoto exclaimed, turning back to face her. It was patently clear in his eyes
that he was very upset by this news. “She was arrested at the scene! We know she was there!”
“Yes, you and I do, but the context of her presence there is now missing,” Mafuyu pointed out. “On
top of that, Sawashiro’s wound, as you know, was determined to be self-inflicted by the doctors at
Touto University Hospital. Because of all of these factors, our office is now investigating the
possibility that the entire thing was a frame-up, and that Sano’s murder was actually the result of an
internal dispute. We believe this is the key reason Sawashiro recanted his testimony.”
“I know the real reason you want this case dropped,” Yamamoto said with an accusatory tone. “You
don’t want to see Takayuki Yagami thrown in jail. Is that it? Drop his charges if you wish. I don’t
care about him. But we cannot let the masterminds get away with this murder!”
Fujii seemed unbothered by this accusation. “I've recused myself from all proceedings related to
Yagami and Kaito,” she revealed. “I have not been present for any deliberations regarding their
cases, and my office will confirm this if you ask. My personal feelings are not a factor here.
“Speaking of masterminds… Were you aware that we initially investigated Masataka Ebina as a
potential suspect?”
Yamamoto shrugged. “I suppose not, but it makes sense.”
“Yes… we happened to check his call logs,” Mafuyu said. “It seems… that he made several calls to
your personal phone over the last year.” She stepped closer, a somewhat predatory look in her own
eyes. “What exactly did the two of you talk about?”
“What are you getting at?”
“I’m merely disclosing what we uncovered. It may be something that comes up in the future, so… I
just wanted to give you a heads up.”
“Are you threatening me, Fujii?” She did not answer, causing him to sigh, bored with the
conversation. “If you must know, Ebina is planning to dissolve the Seiryu Clan,” Yamamoto

answered. “He sought counseling from the police department on the matter, and we've spoken
privately several times about the legalities of such a move.”
Mafuyu glanced at Yamamoto’s gloved hand, which she speculated hid a missing digit from his
days in the yakuza. “Well then. If that’s all, I need to get back to the office.” She bowed, turned
around, and walked towards the door. She opened it, then left, leaving Yamamoto alone in his
office.

her for a moment, then quickly snapped his head back to Kasuga. His thoughts couldn’t be

Well… I guess as long as he doesn’t break character, it’s fine… Kasuga thought to himself. But
man, is this cutting things close. Hanawa-san would shit a brick if he knew this was happening.
“Attention, everyone!” Hironaka announced, walking to the front of the crowd. “We will now be
doing a question and answer session with the Ono Michios and the cast of Featherman R! Of
course, many story details about the upcoming crossover film are still under wraps, so please keep
in mind they won’t be able to answer anything too specific. Now then, anyone who has a question
for the cast, please form an orderly line at the microphone, and they will get to you in the order
you’ve queued!”
“Uh oh,” Haruka muttered. “I don’t know anything about my character.”
“Just avoid going into detail and you’ll be fine,” Pink Argus assured her. “Besides, they mostly just
ask behind-the-scenes questions at these things, so you could probably just make something up.”
“Okay…” She turned to Ono Michio. “Well, are you ready?”
“Y-yeah…” Ono Michio replied, sounding much more nervous than before.
“Huh? Are you okay, mister?”

“I’m fine.”
The fans formed a queue, and soon the first question was asked. A small boy in a Red Hawk mask
approached the microphone. “Hi, my question is for the Featherman R cast… are there any plans
for the previous Rangers to make appearances in the new season?”
Pink Argus leaned into her microphone, which she shared with Haruka. “Hi! Yes, the cast of
Featherman Victory, the 2012 series, filmed material with us for a two-part episode last month. It’s
mostly an episode for your parents, but we hope this generation will also appreciate the
performances of the previous cast. Pink Argus in particular gave a stellar return performance.”
“Gee, I wonder which series you were in…?” Haruka chuckled.
Pink Argus chuckled as well. “Heh… You gotta be your own biggest fan.”
“And also, will Black Condor and Pink Argus finally get together this season?”
“No comment.”
“Thank you for your time.” The boy returned to his spot in the audience, and the next fan
approached the microphone.
“Hi, Ono Michio. Big fan. What was it like joining the set of a big budget theatrical blockbuster?
And also, are you worried about the film’s simultaneous international debut on streaming harming
global box office numbers?”
What the fuck is ‘streaming’? Kiryu thought to himself. Deciding to take an educated guess based
on the context, he answered “Ono Michio is not concerned with the numbers, because Ono Michio
has one goal, and one goal only; to entertain! And I feel like we’ve done just that with this film,
michi. But I will say… anyone who ‘streams’ on this film should take a long look at themselves in
the mirror and wonder just what actions they’ve taken to lead themselves down such a disgusting
path. There are kids here!”
The fan tilted his head in confusion. “Uh… what?”
Haruka knew she needed to save the situation. “What he means is, fans who wish to truly support
the film the best they can should see it in theaters on day one, if they are able, michi! And to our
international fans, we hope that the increased availability of our film in the streaming age helps you
develop an appreciation of Japanese culture!”
“And to add to that,” Pink Argus added, “if I’m not mistaken, this will be the first time that any
Featherman R installment is made available in the west in its original, unedited form.”
Haruka turned to Pink Argus. “Really?”
“Yes. Up until now, all of the western localizations of the franchise have been re-edited,
recontextualized, and had new material shot with American actors,” Pink Argus explained. “My
hope is that this film will draw more attention internationally to the original productions. So if
you’re an international fan watching at home, and you enjoy this movie, go online and watch the
originals! I promise, you won’t be disappointed.”
This sentiment drew agreement from the rest of the Rangers.

Finally, an older fan, a skinny man maybe in his late teens or early twenties, with glasses and chinlength hair, dressed head to toe in various otaku merchandise, approached the microphone. Glaring
at Haruka, he asked “Yeah, my question is for Ono Michiyo. What’s it like being a complete
fraud?!”
Haruka was taken aback by the question. “Um… excuse michi?”
“The entire premise of your new series runs contrary to the established lore of the original!” the
man exclaimed. “You can’t be Ono Michio’s daughter!”
“And why not?”
“Because the settled canon is very clear! Ono Michio… is a VIRGIN! He said so himself at an
appearance in Onomichi six years ago! I should know! I was there!”
Haruka, struggling to comprehend, just stared at the fan. “Why would he have said that,” she said
flatly. “It’s a children’s show.”
“Um… whoops,” Ono Michio muttered under his breath.
The fan continued, angrily, “The way I see it, Ono Michiyo is a woke, DEI plant, designed by
corporate suits to add diversity where there doesn’t need to be any! What do you have to say for
yourself, WHOREno Michiyo?!”
Haruka quickly racked her brain, searching for ways to salvage this situation. Woke? DEI?! What
do any of these words mean?! She didn’t want to anger any fans and potentially harm the film’s
theatrical run. Then, drawing from her own life, she found the answer. “This series doesn’t
contradict any established canon, michi,” she said confidently.
“Huh? How?!”
“You see… Ono Michio is a virgin,” Haruka explained. “That is still true. The truth is… Ono
Michiyo… is ADOPTED!” she revealed dramatically, causing the crowd to gasp.
“R-really?!” the fan asked, shocked.
“Yes. She is,” Haruka explained. “You see, family… It’s not who you’re related to. Rather, family
is the people who are there for you, no matter what, michi.”
Ono Michio turned to Haruka. “Huh?”
“Family can be anything,” she continued. “Friends… co-workers… and yes, relatives, but not
necessarily. I… I know a girl who never knew her biological family. Her mother, her father… both
of them passed when she was very young. She had no brothers or sisters to speak of, at least not
any that she was aware of, or really even cared to know. But there was a man, a strong and kind
man, from a… we’ll say troubled background, who took her in as if he were her own. He cared for
her even when he didn’t have to… and in time, she grew to love him as if he were her own father.
And my life is much the same. To me… Ono Michio… is family.”
“Haruka…” Ono Michio muttered under his breath, too quiet to be heard.
The angry fan’s face softened. “That’s… that’s so beautiful!” he cried out, driven to tears by her
story. Many in the crowd also started to weep. Even Kasuga wiped a tear from his eye.

“Damn, Haruka-chan,” he said. “That’s really something. And you know what? I can relate.” He
thought back to Masumi Arakawa and Jiro Kasuga… and the young master and Sawashiro, too,
even though they didn’t get along a lot. They were all a family. And even though most of them
were gone by that point, there was still one left that he knew he’d see again. Heh… Hey,
Sawashiro… Next time we see each other, the Peking duck is on me.
With a sniffle, Pink Argus leaned in to whisper to Haruka. “Good answer, Ono Michiyo,” she
chuckled, hoping to mask that she, too, had been brought to tears as she thought about her own
found family, all of whom were in the crowd as well, cheering her on.
Well, all except for one, anyway.
The rest of the question and answer segment proceeded without incident, and soon, the event was
coming to a close. The group took a photo together one last time—Ono Michio and Michiyo in the
center performing their signature poses, with the Phoenix Rangers in combat stances fanned out on
either side—and it was all finally over. The crowd started to disperse, and the cast was left alone.
“Phew… that was hard work,” Haruka sighed as Hironaka and Kasuga approached the group.
“But ya did good, Haruka-chan,” Kasuga congratulated with a thumbs up. “And everyone else did,
too!”
“That was PHENOMENAL!” Hironaka gushed. “I just got off the phone with my bosses in Tokyo.
They want to take Ono Michiyo on TOUR next year! Today, Japan. Tomorrow: the world!”
“All of that from one show, huh?” Pink Argus asked. The other Rangers had taken their helmets off
by this point, but she remained in hers. “Damn, Haruka, you really should go back into showbiz.”
“Hehe… I’m glad you think so,” Haruka chuckled, blushing… partly due to embarrassment, but
mostly because it was hot as hell in the costume. “Hang on…” She sighed in relief as she pulled her
headpiece off and fanned cold air onto her face with her hand. “So, what’s next for everyone else?”
“Well, filming just wrapped for me,” Pink Argus sighed. “So I’m leaving Osaka tonight. I’m gonna
miss the food here…”
“And what about you?” Haruka asked, turning to Ono Michio.
“Me…?” Ono Michio asked.
“Hey, why don’t you take off the helmet? It’s gotta be hot in there.”
“…I can’t. For you see… my head is attached to my body!”
“H-huh?!”
Ono Michio stood up and spoke with gravitas, posing triumphantly. “And I must be off! For
wherever there is a child to be made to smile… I must be there! With my charming hassaku face!
Steaming Onomichi ramen hat! Cute fish pouch! Cool boots, vital for any fisherman! And my bold
and trendy Ono shirt! I am the pride of Onomichi… Ono… Michio!” He then went on his way,
marching proudly away and not looking back. Heh… Keep making me proud, Haruka, he thought
as he put more and more distance between himself and her.
“…Some people get too into their characters,” Pink Argus sighed.

~Substory End~

A piece of trash crunched under Joongi Han’s boot as he walked a seemingly empty alleyway in
Osaka’s warehouse district. He had told Kiryu he was searching for information, but truthfully? He

gather information on the side.
And yet, so far, he was coming up short. Tempting as it was to call Seonhee and seek guidance, he
couldn’t bring himself to do so. It would have been a projection of weakness, or that was what his
years in the Jingweon Mafia had taught him, anyway.

can’t sneak up on a shadow,” he muttered underneath his breath as he slowly reached into his

the gun out in front of him and turned a corner, barrel pointed directly at what would be a forehead,
if the person he had been confronting were an adult man.

“I’m going to protect you… and I’m going to get you home,” Joongi reiterated. “I promise.”

Chapter 70: Plume of Dusk
Chapter Notes

Early on in the story, I toyed with the idea of creating storytelling screenshots for big moments
by modding, among other characters, Haruka over Chitose in Infinite Wealth, but quickly gave
up on that idea once I realized that the Okinawa scenes would all be impossible to do, due to
there being no Ryukyu map in Dragon Engine. If only I had waited just a bit longer...

The party braced for action as Ares took a step forward, then let out a skyward metallic screech that
could almost be mistaken for a roar. He charged, and swung, at Kasuga, who beat the attack off
with his bat. He swung at Saeko and Nanba; Saeko effortlessly rolled over his arm, while Nanba
ducked under it. He sent a push kick to Adachi and Zhao, who sidestepped it, sending his foot into
the wall. Joongi and Seonhee each pulled out a pistol and shot at his leg. Sparks flew as the bullets
made contact with the metal.
Enraged, Ares then set his sights on Haruka. His left arm opened up, servos whining as the plates
receded, revealing a rather long katana, sparking with energy; he pulled the katana out with his
right hand, then swung vertically at Haruka, who ducked underneath the attack. He then stabbed at
her, but she quickstepped away from the attack. Stepping toward her, he swung at her legs, and she
jumped up and over the attack, back flipping on her way down, her ponytail trailing behind her.
She managed to jump high enough to make eye contact with him. His comprehension failed him
when he realized she didn’t look frightened; she looked confident, her eyes narrowed and her
mouth curling into a smirk.
PROJECT ARES
Fourth Generation Anti-Shadow Suppression Weapon
Haruka landed on her feet and quickstepped backwards as Ares transformed, and the battle began
anew. Ares shifted his stance, lowering his center of gravity. His left foot slid forward, while his
right anchored behind him, and he angled his katana outward, pointing the tip straight at the party.
His off-hand hovered open at the blade’s pommel. It was a stance that spoke of ruthless precision…
and one Adachi recognized immediately.
“Well I’ll be damned,” he muttered. “Looks like Orbot over here’s got some culture behind his
menace.”

“That stance… that’s Tennen Rishin-ryu.”
“Uh… What’s that?” Haruka asked.

Adachi looked at her, ready to educate. “It’s an old kenjutsu from the Edo period. It was practiced

now.”

Chapter 74: Thicker Than Water Despite Itself
The hum of Akame’s server racks filled the silence. The flickering monitors cast a blue glow over

about the room. Kasuga sat slumped against the wall, nursing a split lip with an ice cold can of
Boss Coffee. Nanba dabbed antiseptic on one of his own wounds. Saeko kicked off her heels, one

for a safety pin, which she threaded neatly into the strap. “That’ll hold until I can get to a shoe
store…”
Yagami and Kaito watched Akame’s monitors, surveilling all of Sotenbori, although they were
unsure what they were looking for; they simply figured they had to do something useful. Adachi,

just… watching her.
Haruka hadn’t said a word since they got back. She simply sat near Haruto, watching as he slept.
Akame arrived with a cup of hot water. “Drink. You haven’t had anything to drink all night. Am I
right?”
Haruka chuckled softly. “No, I guess not. Thanks.” She took the mug and sipped carefully.

“I don’t really think this is what Haruka-chan needs to hear right now,” Adachi chimed in.

Haruka studied Seonhee, who had a serious look in her eyes… though she noticed a slight smile

hair back.

Just half an hour earlier, Kiryu, still dressed in his Daidoji Faction getup—black shirt, charcoal
slacks, black loafers, and that unfortunate bowl cut—arrived at the Cabaret Grand with Hanawa,

Taichi scoffed. “Nice act, man.”
Hanawa rolled his eyes. “Just trying to end the night peacefully before I have to get back to kissing
Viper’s ass. Relax, would you?”
In truth, however, this was an act, though not in the way anyone would have expected. There was

wouldn’t be an ass left to kiss…

Chapter 75: KATATOKI
The Grand was exactly as Kiryu remembered it, which he supposed made sense; it was, of course,
among the oldest entertainment establishments in Sotenbori, having opened prior to the Second
World War. This resulted in it being the most permanent and consistent fixture in Osaka’s nightlife
district—as such, very little had changed, physically, since Kiryu’s last visit in 2006.
Despite this, however, the air itself felt different as the group entered. A hostess in a crimson gown
bowed gracefully—“Welcome!”—and led them to their table on the second floor, a half-moon
booth overlooking the stage, where, quite unusually for this cabaret, there appeared to be an
American man getting ready to perform. He had dark skin with short dreads underneath a black hat
with the word “ATLANTA” emblazoned on the front, as well as a variety of tattoos crawling up his
neck. He conversed with a Japanese man, who also appeared to be a performer as their crew set up
a variety of electronic equipment, keyboards, drums, and such.
Kiryu watched the men set their performance up with interest. “Not the kind of entertainment I’m
used to seeing here,” he murmured. Glancing around, and seeing a lot of younger people seated
throughout the establishment, he added “Not the crowd I’d have expected either. The last time I
was here, the Grand’s clientele skewed older, stuffier, more professional. Suits, politicians, and
yakuza. This… This is the sort of crowd I’d have expected in a nightclub, or at a concert.”
“You don’t like it?” Hanawa asked.
Kiryu shrugged. “Actually, I… find it sort of refreshing. These people seem like… people. It’s
nice.” He nodded his head towards the performers. “Still, that guy on stage… Who’s he?
“I believe the Japanese man is Yojiro Noda,” Hanawa said quietly as he gestured to the Japanese
man, who said something that made the American laugh. “Frontman of RADWIMPS. He’s the
main act. Performing some new material tonight.”
“A record premiere in a cabaret?” Kiryu asked. “That hardly seems practical.”
“On the contrary, Kiryu… Half of the people here are here for the act.” Hanawa chuckled. “The
times are changing, and old farts like us… we’re being left behind.”
“That’s not always a bad thing,” Kiryu noted.
“No, it is not.”
“What about the American?” Kiryu asked.
Hanawa shook his head. “Not sure. I hear he’s very popular in the States recently though.”
“JID,” Taichi suddenly chimed in from behind them. “His name’s on a poster out front. He’s a
rapper.”
Kiryu glanced at Hanawa, then back at Taichi. “…You know him?”
Taichi shrugged. “Kind of? I don’t understand a word he says—my English sucks—but it’s catchy.
He’s all over the internet right now.”

Hanawa smirked and looked back at Kiryu. “There you go.”

Across from them, Taichi and Sugiura made room as another, slightly younger-looking hostess in a

On the ground floor, the lights began to dim, and the American motioned to his sound crew. The

“One man walking alone
Lost in a land running from home.
One chance righting the wrongs
No one understands him.”
The Japanese singer grabbed his own mic and cut in with the same cadence, same rhythm, same
story, but in his own tongue,
“Machi ka teiru kado
Kagami shirubeto.
Nantei takoro no
Sora wa toiu nai yo.”
The drummer switched the beat up as a snare loop kicked in through the speakers to compliment
his own work. The American rapper dove straight into his verse,
“You’re not the man ‘til you beat the master
You got the plan, then we get to action
I got the answers to what you’re askin’
But can you handle a hand-to-hand…”
The music filled the Grand as the rapper flowed effortlessly through his verse with an almost
mournful tone… and to Kiryu, it sounded strangely personal. One man walking alone, he repeated

to himself internally as he took in the song. A line so nonspecific and, frankly, so generic it could

He glanced at his own reflection in a glass divider separating this booth from its unoccupied

own graying hair, and he ran a hand through his stupid bowl cut that he had claimed was growing
on him. The truth was, he hated it. It wasn’t him. And as he looked back into his own eyes, he no
longer saw a dragon behind them. Just a tired, cowardly old man, trying to erase a past that shamed
him while burning everyone he loved along the way.
He unconsciously pushed his hair back. It more closely resembled his old haircut like this. He
wanted that back. He wanted to be himself again.
“Kiryu?” Hanawa said, interrupting his thoughts. “You okay?”
Kiryu slowly turned his head to Hanawa and dropped his hand, letting his hair fall back into the

Taichi shook his head. “But—!”

The pinnacle of prestige champagne, Ace of Spades is produced by the Cattier family in the village

of care they give to the environment to protect it for future generations. So while your drink tonight

Hanawa frowned and leaned back in his seat. “And why shouldn’t I be for one night? Soma’s going

Chapter 76: The Dragon of Dojima

Rolling eyes fall…

Ruling dies out…

Moments later, Kiryu stood in a dressing room, staring at his reflection in the mirror. He had
donned the pants and the loafers, but had yet to put the top on; instead, he stood shirtless in the

room, his rippled muscles, a result of literal decades of fighting, staring back at him. The skin

Chapter 77: Receive You The Unwavering
As Kiryu beat back Yagami and Kaito’s kicks, their legs crashing against his forearms like steel
against steel, something stirred within him.
It wasn’t anger.
It wasn’t pride.
It was clarity.
It was a REVELATION.
If the Dragon was making a comeback, then so too must his fighting style be reborn. By combining
the grit of a brawler, the speed and precision of a boxer, the raw, terrifying strength of the beast
within, and the controlled brutality of an agent, as well as some old moves from his youth, Kiryu
believed he could finally perfect the ultimate, final form of all of his fighting styles—Dragon of
Dojima: Kiwami. He switched into this fighting style, his stance identical to his Yakuza style, and
exhaled.
“Let’s end this quickly,” he said, more to himself than to them.
Kaito lunged at him with a wild right hook; Kiryu sidestepped this and countered with a hook to his
ribs, then followed up with a roundhouse kick to the face. Gathering all of his strength, he then
charged up a wide right hook, a wide left hook, and a left back fist into a right overhead swing,
which bounced Kaito off of the ground, briefly suspending him in the air. He finished the combo
with a right hook, a left mid kick, and a right wheel kick that sent Kaito sprawling to the ground.

Chapter 83: Cold War
Kazuki Soma’s escort glided through the midnight traffic, the engine humming steadily as he left
Osaka’s city limits and headed east, towards Kanagawa. Soma himself lounged in the back seat,
one leg crossed over the other, as he sipped on red wine. “Oh, driver?” he said. “How long until
Isezaki Ijincho?”
The driver glanced at his GPS. “A little over five hours, now that we’ve hit the expressway. Might
as well try and get some rest. I’ll let you know when we cross into Kanagawa Prefecture.”
Soma chuckled, and sipped his wine. “I quite like a night drive, actually. I might just watch the
cities pass us by.”
The driver nodded. “As you wish, sir.”
Everything was proceeding nicely. Soma had established total dominance over Kihei Hanawa, who
folded like wet paper, and Kazuma Kiryu, who was easily leashed once he knew what was at stake.
Chihiro Watanabe would be recovered soon enough. Kiryu, he knew, would be unable to kill her.
The so-called “Dragon” lacked the stomach to do the job. He was weak. That was fine. Soma
would do it himself, gladly.
Cleaning up messes was what he was best at, after all.
He allowed himself a small, self-satisfied sigh as he leaned back into his seat. His new career was
already going along swimmingly. He held his smartphone up to his face as he took another sip,
deciding to catch himself up on what had been happening in Kanto since his imprisonment and
subsequent recruitment by the Daidoji, settling on an article from the Tokyo-based news site
“Kamuro Daily”.
LITTLE ASIA REVIVAL PROJECT NEARS COMPLETION
A photograph of Tokyo’s governor, Saori Yoshida, standing beside Tokyo MPD CommissionerGeneral Akio Yamamoto, sat beneath the headline.
More than six years after the alleged yakuza-backed arson attack on Shinjuku’s Little Asia, for
which no suspect was ever apprehended, Tokyo Governor Saori Yoshida announces the district is
finally ready to reopen.
“We’re proud to say that we will be cutting the ribbon on this project, which has been years in the
making, next week,” Governor Yoshida said during a press conference with TMPD Commissioner
Akio Yamamoto (pictured above) this morning. “In completing this project, Kamurocho has won its
war against organized crime.”
Soma scoffed, but continued reading.
Organized crime and government corruption have been two areas of intense interest for the
Governor as she seeks to move past the shadow cast by the scandalous tenure of her predecessor,
the late Ryo Aoki, who was assassinated at the height of his scandals in 2019.

Yoshida, formerly aligned with Aoki through Bleach Japan before renouncing the group after his
assassinstion, won the 2020 election to replace him in an extraordinarily narrow three-way race
with then-ruling coalition backing, and she has struggled to guide Tokyo through the tumultuous
aftermath. Though sidetracked early on by the pandemic, her early and aggressive response to that
crisis helped carve her out as a decisive and effective leader. In 2021, she restarted the Little Asia
Revival Project, which had been quietly shelved by Aoki in 2018.
“Little Asia had long been a hub for criminal activity in Kamurocho,” Yoshida said of the old
district. “With the help of the TMPD, led by Commissioner Yamamoto, we’re ensuring it can be a
place to raise a family going forward.”
Though the Governor and the Commissioner have a warm public relationship, insiders claim things
are a bit frostier behind the scenes, with Yamamoto rumored to be weighing a run against the
incumbent in 2024. Governor Yoshida, for her part, has grown increasingly frustrated with the
failure of the TMPD to apprehend suspected yakuza Haruka Sawamura and Masaharu Kaito.
Yamamoto as well has his own frustrations regarding the case; many of the other suspects in
Sawamura’s alleged murder of Seiryu Clan yakuza Hachiro Sano have had charges dismissed by
the Ministry of Justice, which Yamamoto has privately decried as an “embarrassment”.
Tokyo District Chief Prosecutor Mafuyu Fujii, who is personally overseeing Sawamura’s
prosecution, declined to comment, citing the ongoing investigation. Deputy Chief Prosecutor Sae
Niijima, herself no stranger to controversy, similarly declined to comment on her prosecution of
Kaito.
Despite this, public confidence in the TMPD remains unusually high, with many Tokyo residents
crediting Yamamoto’s tenure for maintaining post-pandemic order. Under Commissioner
Yamamoto, the TMPD has expanded its mandate through a series of security initiatives approved
this year, though critics and some constitutional scholars say certain provisions may run contrary
to Article 9 of the Constitution; similar criticisms have been made with regards to the Self-Defense
Forces since the turn of the century.
FOR YOU: Several Prefectures Question NPA Handling of Sawamura Case

Bull. Uber Eats. An especially massive vertical billboard advertised SEGA’s Sonic Frontiers, which
had released the prior month. And plastered over the 705 itself…
FUTURE LOOKING DARK? JOIN BLEACH JAPAN TODAY!
MOST CRIMINAL CONVICTIONS NOT DISQUALIFYING!
WWW.NPA.GO.JP/BLEACHJAPAN
Kasuga’s eyes widened. “Bleach Japan…?” That resurfaced some bad memories. “The young
master’s old organization? I thought it was banned. Why is it back?! A-and why are they plastered
on the biggest billboard in town?!”
Yagami narrowed his eyes at the billboard. “And I thought the name was political suicide
anyway… The governor had to renounce her affiliation to even stand a chance in the election. Now
she’s loud and proud about it? Something smells…”
Kaito grumbled, “Who’da thunk? Kamurocho’s stench has wafted all the way out here…”
“I wonder if Higashi knows anything about it,” Yagami said. “We should call him, see if he’s
learned anything else.” He pulled out his phone, scrolled to Higashi’s name, and tapped the screen.
The phone rang.
And rang.
…And rang.

“Hm… he’s not answering…” he muttered.
Kaito shrugged. “It’s late, Tak. He’s probably fast asleep. Anyway.” He turned around and gestured
to the city around him. “Welcome to Hachikocho, everyone. The center of Shibuya. The
commercial capital of Tokyo. Fashion, music, movies, it all runs through here. It’s loud, it’s bright,
and it’s where all the kids hang out. Man, you shoulda seen the Tojo families that had territory out
here back in the day. Those guys were makin’ MONEY, runnin’ record labels, financin’ nightclubs,
and rubbing elbows with the political elites.”
He gestured across the Scramble. “That’s Central Street, over there. It’s where we’re gonna do all
of our shopping, if we have to do shopping while we’re here. My guess is Kamurocho is a bad
fucking idea right now, so I’m going to suggest that we stick around this area, at least for now. With
that being said, Kamurocho’s north, past Shinjuku Station. Yongen-Jaya’s west, into the suburbs.
They’re both maybe ten minutes by cab, less if traffic is kind.”
Kasuga approached a bronze statue of an Akita dog, which sat on a pedestal across from the station.
“What’s this for?”
Kaito followed. “Ah, this is Hachiko-san himself. Back before the war, he had an owner that used
to commute to Bunkyo, and Hachiko-san would wait for him at the station every evening. One day,
the guy died at work, and Hachiko waited here all night for an owner that never showed. Even
though they’d only been together about a year, Hachiko spent the next ten years comin’ by the
station, same time every day, and waitin’ to see if that owner would show up. Obviously, he never
did.
“His story became a national inspiration, and they erected a statue in his honor. Technically, this
one ain’t the original, but this is the spot he would wait at. Yup, this little guy was probably more
loyal to his owner than anyone else in this town is to anyone they know.”
Yagami raised an eyebrow. “…Are you crying, Kaito-san?”
“Hell yeah I am! This dog’s the only decent creature in the whole city!”
Kasuga smiled at the statue. “A decade waitin’ for someone who meant the world to you, huh?
Good shit, Hachiko-san.”
The statue, of course, said nothing.

The party walked through the streets, which became less dense as they got closer to their
destination. “Y’know, I never got addresses,” Kasuga said. “I always just went by landmarks. Just
tell me it’s near a cafe under a bridge or something. Numbers make things too complicated.”
Yagami chuckled. “You wanna hear a secret? They’re not for us. They’re for postmen.”
Kasuga nodded. “That makes sense, I guess.”
Kaito glanced up at a street sign as they walked under. “Shimo-Meguro… not much farther now.
Yongen-Jaya’s the next neighborhood over.”

“You know, I hear a lot of celebrities live in this part of the city,” Kasuga said. “I guess it makes
sense, if crime is as low as you say.”
“Yeah, everyone around here has money out the ass,” Kaito explained. “You’d think that means
there’s a lot of rich marks for thugs to prey on, but it actually just means everyone can afford to sue
the fuck out of you if you try to start shit. They also don’t really spend their money here. They
spend it in Shibuya. Hence why a yakuza isn’t going to profit much from running a front here.”
He smirked. “Heh… although… this place is remindin’ me of a little story from my Tojo days…”
Haruka smiled. “Ooh, are we going to hear about Kaito-san’s youth?” she asked in a higher register,
clasping her hands together.
“Ya say that like I’m old now!” Kaito replied, annoyed. “I’m only… 42… Ah, shit…” He shook his
head. “Anyway. This wasn’t actually that long ago. Woulda been… 2016? About a year before
Matsugane gave me the boot and I joined Tak at the detective agency.
“See, that whole year, somethin’… weird was going on. Random people all over Tokyo were havin’
breakdowns, just completely losing their shit and going bananas in public. One guy went viral on
the internet after he stripped naked and started dancing in an intersection. Another was doing some
unhinged shit behind the counter in a Wild Jackson’s. Just… really bizarre psychotic breaks.
“Around the same time that started happening, a buncha rich and powerful people started losing
their shit in a different way.” He frowned. “This stuff was… unsettling. Guys would be fine one
day, and then would just… break down in tears the next. Sobbing. Confessing crimes and begging
for forgiveness. I mean, I don’t scare easy, but that? That was chilling. One of them, some fast food
CEO or something like that, started confessing to abusing his workers… and then died.”
Kasuga raised an eyebrow. “Did he off himself?”
Kaito shook his head. “Nah. Like, dropped dead. Right there. Heart attack, midway through the
press conference, on live television.”
“Holy shit…” Kasuga muttered, shuddering. “Talk about bad timing.”
“Yeah. It was freaky as hell. Some kinda divine retribution shit.” Kaito shrugged. “Anyway. All of
these rich assholes had one thing in common; all of them had been targeted the night before by
some blackmail gang.”
Yagami snapped his fingers. “Ohhh, I remember this now. Yeah. That was weird.”
“I just don’t get it,” Kasuga said, scratching his head. “So, what, somebody tells them they have
dirt on them, and they try to get ahead of the story?”
Kaito shrugged. “Could be. But, the way these guys were acting, you’d think the blackmailers were
holding some scary shit over them. It became a national story. Every single month, one of these
guys would get a calling card, and the next day, they’re spillin’ their guts and bawling on TV.

Eventually, the police announced a manhunt trying to catch these guys… but they operated without
a trace. No prints, no signs of entry, no nothin’.
“Now, some people in the Tojo Clan started to get a little nervous,” he continued. “The Sixth
Chairman didn’t seem worried, but some of the other patriarchs? They were real worried. And… I
gotta admit, I never really cared about clan politics… but I was worried about the boss.
Matsugane… he was a good guy. I didn’t know if the blackmailers were goin’ after specific guys,
or just criminals in general. And looking back… MAYBE I overreacted. All of those other guys
were bad dudes, and besides, it’s not like pops was very visible. But still, I was worried. So… I
started doin’ a little sleuthing of my own.”
Kasuga would have been on the edge of his seat if he had a seat. “What’d you find?”
“First off, I put together a list of victims,” Kaito explained. “I don’t remember off the top of my
head who everyone was, except that at that point the latest one was that food CEO. People were
sayin’ the blackmailers killed him. I think it was just bad timing.”
He waved that off, because frankly, the thought made him shiver. “I ended up deducing that the first
victim, or one of the first, was an Olympic volleyball player who was teachin’ at a local high
school. Ahhhh, Shujin Academy, I think it was. Not far from Shibuya either. Most of the targets
were around that area, so it’s pretty easy to assume that they were based in or around Shibuya.
“Anyway. This teacher… was a real scumfuck, let me tell you something.” His face hardened. He
actually looked angry. “The things he did… I hope he gets his ass beat in prison every single day.”
His face softened. “But, here’s where it gets weird… He wasn’t on anybody’s radar at the time. He
had his moment in the spotlight, and things were pretty quiet for him after. Which means…
whoever ran this gang had to be intimately aware of his crimes for them to be blackmailing him
like that. This wasn’t a ‘we found some dirt, let’s use it’ kinda deal. It was personal. He hurt
somebody in or around that gang, and they took their revenge. So I figured out that the head
honchos came from that school. Hell, maybe they were even students.”
“This seems… impossible to believe,” Haruka said.
“It gets weirder,” Kaito continued. “See, the trail went cold after that. I couldn’t find anything else.
And about a month later, cops are saying they got the ringleader in a sting operation. Next day, he’s
dead in custody. Apparently, he stole a guard’s gun, killed him, and then blew his own shit
smooth.”
“Jesus,” Kasuga muttered.
“So that’s the end of that, right?” Kaito asked rhetorically. “Hehe. You would think. Because as it
so happens, I checked that school’s roster afterwards. That year, no teachers dropped off the roster.
The headmaster died, but he got hit by a truck or some shit like that. Totally unrelated. And only
two students dropped off the roster. One of them, a girl I think, transferred schools midway through
the year. The other was only gone for about a month, and then returned after Christmas to finish out
the year.
“And then one month later… the group strikes again.” He grinned. “The victim? Masayoshi Shido,
the newly elected Prime Minister of Japan. The highest profile target they could pick.”
“Some kinda revenge hit?” Kasuga asked.

Kaito shook his head. “Nah. You remember what I said? The leader had to come from that school,
and nobody was permanently dropped from the roster. You ask me? The suicide was a ruse. Cops
trying to save face after months of investigation with no payoff. That kid… they’re still out there
somewhere.”
He looked around, his grin slowly returning as they entered Yongen-Jaya proper. “You know where
I’d be hiding out, if I was that kid?” He gestured vaguely around. “A place where nobody’s gonna
be lookin’ for me. A place where the cops and the yakuza don’t even bother. A place… just like
Yongen-Jaya.” He chuckled. “Who knows? Maybe he’s hidin’ around the corner… waiting to
strike. Taking. His. Time.”
Kasuga shuddered. “Ugh! You know, Kaito-san, you really know how to spin a tale!”
Kaito got a serious look on his face. “A tale? You go and tell yourself that… if it helps ya sleep at
night.” He smirked and stopped in front of an unassuming cafe. “Hmph. Alright. This should be the
place.”
Haruka looked up at the sign. “Leblanc…” she read aloud. “What is this? A coffee shop?”
Kaito crossed his arms. “Looks like it.”
“It says they’re closed,” Kasuga said.
Kaito turned the knob, and the door came open. “Door’s unlocked.” He waved the others in. “After
you.”
Haruka stepped in first, and the others followed. It was a dimly lit cafe that smelled of coffee and
curry. As soon as she walked in, she took notice of a painting on the wall to her right. A woman in
red held a baby, with a sparsely flowered cherry blossom branch behind her. A small plaque sat
beneath the framed painting.
Sayuri
Unknown artist c. 2001
“Huh, I think I’ve seen this one before,” Yagami commented. “Pretty convincing replica, I gotta
say.”
“Can’t you read the sign?” a gruff voice from an unseen source said, drawing the party’s attention.
A middle-aged man with slicked back graying black hair, a receding hairline, and a sharply
trimmed chinstrap beard came around the corner. He wore half-rimmed glasses and an apron, and
he did not look amused. “We’re closed.”
A young man who appeared to be in his early 20s rounded the corner as well, also wearing an
apron. He was of slightly above average height and was pale with unkempt, wavy black hair that
fell over his eyes. He wore a large pair of glasses over his sharp eyes; the thin sliver of room that
could be seen through his lenses lacked any sort of noticeable distortion, so Haruka surmised the
glasses themselves were fake.
She looked at the older man. “Um… we were told to come here…” she said softly. “Are you the
one who called us?”

His eyes widened slightly. “Hm? Wait… you actually came?”
Kaito glared at him. “So it was you.”
“Actually,” a female voice said from the corner of the room, “it was me.” The party turned their
attention to a booth that they had failed to notice was occupied. She was a tall, pretty young woman
with ashen brown hair, parted on the right side, and reddish eyes—though Haruka could swear
there was a golden glint in them. She wore a black business suit over a black turtleneck, with a
section sign necklace over top of it, and she had quite a serious look in her eyes. “Haruka
Sawamura. You really came.”
The old man sighed, and turned to his protege. “Close up for me when… this is done. Alright?”
The young man nodded. “You got it.” Hanging his apron up, the old man stepped past the party and
out the door, closing it behind him. The young man turned to Haruka with a slight smile. “Can I get
you anything?”
“You should go, too,” the woman said suddenly, to which the boy shook his head.
“I live here,” he said.
The woman rolled her eyes. “Fine.”
Haruka turned to the woman with a hardened glare as the boy went to brew a fresh pot of coffee.
“Who are you? Why did you call us here?”
The woman didn’t answer immediately. She instead took a sip of her coffee. “Sit,” she ordered.
“We have things we need to discuss. In truth, this meeting has been a long time coming.”
“Huh?”
“You’ve been on the run since the murder of Hachiro Sano, and I’m the one who’s been chasing
after you. You see… I’m the woman who’s going to hang you… or set you free.” She looked up at
Haruka with a serious look in her eyes. “Sae Niijima, Ministry of Justice. A pleasure to make your
acquaintance.”

Chapter 94: Le Jugement
Yagami crossed his arms at Sae. “You’re Mafuyu’s deputy at the Ministry of Justice,” he said.
“You’re the one overseeing Kaito-san’s case.”
“And, as of yesterday, Haruka Sawamura’s,” Sae revealed.
Yagami raised an eyebrow. “Hm?”
Sae sighed. “…Fujii has… fled the city.”
“What?!” Yagami exclaimed. “Is she okay?!”
“She’s fine,” Sae replied. “But one of her investigations put the wrong kind of attention on her. She
needs time to pursue that investigation, without interference from bad actors. So she assigned the
Sawamura case to me and left Tokyo. There are less eyes on me. A lot less. That’s actually a
miracle, all things considered…”
Kaito cleared his throat and gestured to the barista behind the counter. “Hey, uh, not to interrupt,
but… is he gonna be a problem?” He stared at the boy. “He’s not gonna talk, is he?”
The boy simply smirked.
“Believe me, he is no friend of the police,” Sae answered. “I chose this location because I knew
nothing said here would leave this room. Now sit. We have a lot to talk about, and I don’t imagine
you’d like to be on your feet the whole time.”
Haruka looked uneasy. “How do we know this isn’t a trap?”
“If it is, you walked into it already,” Sae quipped. “Good job.”
Kasuga grimaced as he and Haruka slid into the booth. “Ah… we kinda did, didn’t we?” he

Yagami and Kaito remained standing. “Just so you know, I’m Haruka’s lawyer,” Yagami revealed,
brandishing his pin. “I might not look it, but I’ve been doing this a while, so don’t try any funny
business.”
“Wouldn’t dream of it, Takayuki Yagami,” Sae replied. The barista came around with a tray of
coffee, placing a cup in front of Sae, Haruka, and Kasuga. “Thank you, Ren.”
He then turned to Yagami and Kaito to offer them coffee. Yagami took a cup—“Thanks.”—but
Kaito simply held a hand up.
“Not a coffee guy, thanks,” he said. The barista nodded and walked back behind the counter.
“Smells good, though,” Kaito added.
Sae sipped her coffee, and was silent for a moment. “…You’re accused of some very serious
crimes, Haruka,” she said quietly. “The murder of Hachiro Sano of the Seiryu Clan. Even under the
most generous circumstances, that crime alone is all but guaranteed to get you ten years or more.

You’re also suspected of leading the Shin Tojo Alliance, a yakuza group operating out of
Kamurocho formed from the ashes of the Tojo Clan. This ups your potential sentence significantly.
You also escaped from police custody, assaulted officers, and have since evaded capture.
“Altogether you could face life in prison. Maybe even the death penalty.” She sipped her coffee
once more and glanced up at Haruka. “If I pursued this case, I would win. I have no doubts about
that. My record is flawless.”
“Almost flawless,” Yagami interrupted. “There was one high profile case in 2016 where you failed
to secure even a single conviction. A blackmail gang terrorized Tokyo, and you were the public
face of that investigation. Your failure to secure a conviction caused you to resign from the
Ministry in disgrace, and in 2017 you opened a defense practice in Shibuya.”
Sae chuckled dryly. “You did your research, Yagami-san. I’m impressed, though unsurprised. After
all… I’m sure the downfall of one of the people who put Shinpei Okubo behind bars for the murder

Yagami’s face didn’t shift. “Truth be told, I thought Okubo was guilty the second time around,” he

“Do you want to hear a secret, Yagami-san?” Sae said. “I rigged that trial, and countless others. I
had no doubts that Okubo would be convicted, not because I felt he was guilty, but because I was

a paper. I suppose you’re lucky you only have that regret. My regrets span my entire career.”
The barista looked up from his work behind the counter, a sad look in his eyes. “Sae…”
Sae shook her head. “That’s why we’re here today. Because I got it wrong before. Not once. Not
twice. Too many times to count.” She inhaled deeply, then let out a long sigh. “And I’m not going

Yagami’s eyes narrowed. “Why’d you rejoin the Ministry, Niijima-san?” he asked.
Sae crossed her arms and leaned back in her seat. “The answer lies in the reason I left the Ministry.
No, it wasn’t because of the one black spot on my record. That entire case opened my eyes. One
could say I had a change of heart. I had done enough harm for a lifetime. I wanted to become the

She leaned forward. “One of my first clients was Daigo Dojima.”
The name dropped like a stone. Kaito’s eyes widened. “The Tojo Clan’s Sixth Chairman?”
She nodded. “Yes. He came to me in 2018. He, along with Goro Majima and Taiga Saejima, had
been in hiding since the year before, which facilitated the takeover of Tokyo by the Omi Alliance,

She glanced at Kasuga. “Your patriarch, correct?”
Kasuga nodded. “Yeah. Only… I had been banished from the clan in 2001, so… I guess he wasn’t

the thousands of yakuza who swore their lives to him would be able to transition back to civilian

“You’re gonna regret pissing me off,” Kaito growled, though he grinned as he did so. Switching to

“Nani miten dayo!” the knife-wielding enemy called out as he approached Sae. Getting ready to

Sae flinched. “Ngh! You little…!” She then took a turn, grabbing him in an aikido chokehold and

“Itee!” the goon grunted as he hit the pavement, which cracked beneath him.
“Play stupid games, win stupid prizes…” she grumbled as she settled into an aikido stance, her

“Heyyyy, the prosecutor’s got some moves!” Kasuga said with a grin.

“Heh. Whatever you say…”
With now five in the party—the core four of Haruka, Ichiban, Yagami, and Kaito, as well as the

A baton goon approached Haruka—“Horitsu o mamore!”—and smacked her across the face with a

One of the unarmed goons approached Yagami in a boxer stance and attacked with a right hook and

Yagami switched to his Tiger style so that he could attack an unarmed enemy with an EX Action.
He stood opposite the enemy, who growled and swung at him. Yagami dodged the attack, sending

Frustrated, the enemy kicked the car, then punched the window. Shortly after, the window rolled

This was when the enemy realized he was probably going to spend the rest of his life working on a

“No! It just… happens, sometimes!”
“Sometimes? As in more than once?”

Knife Goon, who at this point was the last one on the battlefield, made one last effort to detain

This is where Sae came in. She approached Haruka with a move she called Know Your Rights.
“You should know: that was a violation of your rights as a citizen.” This, somehow, cured all of

This allowed Haruka to not take damage when her turn came around, and she ran at the knife goon,

With the last Bleach Japan goon defeated, Sae approached the ex-Nishikiyama Family member,

The man stammered in fear. “A-ah! It’s just us! I swear! W-We were here to arrest the guy that lives

He crossed his fingers behind his back, as if Sae didn’t already know he was completely full of it.

Sae sighed, but didn’t turn. “For the time being, no,” she replied. She fully turned to face the party,

Watching as a car drove down an adjacent alleyway, she found herself slightly, and justifiably,

Ijincho. If anything happens… Come find me. In the meantime, watch your back. Don't trust

“Actually, it’s extraordinarily unpredictable.”
“Fair enough. Stay safe, sis.”

“No time to explain, Inspector Hasegawa. Things are getting bad in Tokyo and I have to leave town

“Say no more. I’m on my way. I was actually already in Yokohama, looking into that Haruka

“Eh. Something about it didn’t pass the smell test anyway. Anyway, don’t worry about it. I’ll make

Sae sighed. “They aren’t kids anymore, Hasegawa.”
Hasegawa groaned. “Agh! Don’t say that, you’ll make me feel… even older than I already do.

Haruka raised an eyebrow. “Who was that?”

Kaito glanced out the window as they hit the highway. He watched as a black car moved into the

SUV.

leaned out his window, firing at the SUV, bullet holes riddling the right side doors. Sae’s eyes

That car swerved and lost traction, spinning out and colliding with the previously damaged car;

Chapter 97: Dark Ties
Akio Yamamoto stood atop a rooftop in central Kamurocho, smoke trailing from a cigarette that
hung loosely between his fingers. It didn’t matter which rooftop; it would all be his soon enough,
he knew as he looked out at the town they called the “armpit of Tokyo”.
He drew the cigarette to his lips and took a drag, pausing as he heard footsteps behind him. He
smirked. “Took you long enough… Mine-chan.”

Yoshitaka Mine was a tall man in his early thirties with a serious face and short, dark brown hair
with a couple of strands that hung loosely over the right side of his face. He wore a black pinstriped
double-breasted suit with a black dress shirt and a gold tie, and held a briefcase in his right hand,
presumably packed with cash for Patriarch Kanda. Adorned on his suit was a small lapel pin
bearing the crest of the Nishikiyama Family, where he had quickly risen the ranks. In fact…
“I hear the boss is giving you your own family,” Yamamoto noted. He chuckled and took another
drag of his cigarette. “And in under a year, too. Funny, how far throwing a little money around and
wagging your tail like an obedient lapdog can get you. I bet your wife is pleased, huh?” Yamamoto
didn’t even wait for a response before laughing at his own joke. “Hah! Right, no wife. Sorry; I
forgot who I was talking to for a second.”
He took yet another drag of his cigarette, adding “You know, once they find out what you are…
your new subordinates are gonna find it real hard to respect you.”
Mine’s grip on the briefcase neither tightened nor loosened, and his face showed no signs of
reaction to Yamamoto’s taunts and jeers. He was silent for a moment. Then, he spoke up: “I know
you’ve been talking to the police.”
Yamamoto froze. “…Oh yeah? You got any proof?”
Mine shook his head. “Nothing concrete, no. Just circumstance and a few hunches. Frankly, it
doesn’t really concern me, now that we're going our separate ways in the Clan.”
“So, what, you’re just making bogus accusations to start shit?”
Mine rolled his head and let out a sigh. “I really don’t care what you do in this family anymore. The
way I see it, you’re Kanda’s problem now. Not mine. But let me be very clear about something.”
He stepped closer, his expression unchanging—which was somehow scarier. “I don’t know what

your end goal is… but if you put the Sixth Chairman—Chairman Dojima—in harm’s way with
your indiscretion… I’ll be forced to do something… unpleasant.”
“I- I’m not scared of a fruit,” Yamamoto replied rather unconvincingly.
Mine nodded. “That’s fine. I’m not here to intimidate. Only to warn.” He turned from Yamamoto
and began to walk back to the stairwell from which he came. “Watch your step, Yamamoto.
Because you aren’t as untouchable as you seem to think you are.”
Yamamoto gripped the railing. “You idiot… Your devotion to Daigo Dojima is going to get you
killed one day.”
Mine paused. “It seems you still don’t understand what this life is about.”
Growling, Yamamoto pushed from the railing and turned to glare at Mine, who slowly turned
around to face him. “What the hell would you know about what it’s like to be a yakuza?”
Mine tilted his head. “You tell me. By this time next week, I will be leading my own clan. That
seems rather authoritative to me. And I also know that I have all ten digits, and you, unfortunately,
do not. Not exactly the mark of a successful career, is it?”
“Not even a year ago you were some trust fund banker or whatever the fuck you were,” Yamamoto
spat. “Then all of a sudden you find out you’ve got a crush, and you just dropped everything and
swore up, just like that? I’ve been in this business for more than a decade! And I do real work,
none of that wire fraud or insider trading bullshit you do.”
“Funny, then, that you seem to have only made lateral moves in that time,” Mine replied instantly.
“Perhaps you should reflect on that.”
“Fuck. You.”
“I’m actually good, thanks.” And with that, Mine turned and walked down the stairs, leaving
Yamamoto to stew in his own misery.
“Fuckin’ prick,” Yamamoto growled as he threw his cigarette down. “Who does he think he is?
He’s a nobody, that’s what. Just a rich kid with Daigo Dojima's cock in his mouth. Fuck him.”
To Yamamoto, it was becoming very clear, however, that Yoshitaka Mine would be a huge pain in
his ass going forward.
…For as long as he remained alive, that was.

Kiryu and Taichi entered Tartarus, a cozy little bar on Hachikocho’s Center Street, located between

exception—a bus stop sign that looked like it had been pulled from the ground hung up on the wall
near the corner, just behind the Joysound setup.

you two to do me a favor,” he said politely. “Figure out how many agents we have in the field. Get
me their names. Get me any leverage we might have. It appears… it has fallen upon me to right the
ship.”
The men, still trembling, nodded. “Y-yes! Right away, sir!” They stood up, and quickly bolted from
the room.
Soma held the phone back up to his face. “I do hope you’re adaptable to change, Hanawa-san,” he
said triumphantly as he walked to the window to stare out at the moonlit forest. “Because changes
are coming. We’ll speak soon. Don’t worry… you don’t have to tell me where you are. I’ll find
you.”
The line went dead, and Hanawa’s face went pale.

pushed past Kiryu and Nishiki and sprinted out of the Empty Lot.
Sawashiro watched him go. The smile vanished the moment he was gone, and he turned to glare at
Kiryu and Nishiki. “Dojima Family, huh?” He circled them once more. “You boys make a habit of
collecting on other families’ turf?”
Nishiki clenched his fists. “W-what’s it to you? It’s none of your business.”
“Oh, it is all of my business,” Sawashiro chuckled. “As the Arakawa Family’s treasurer, well… I
can’t go and embarrass my boss by letting some little punks do business with our clients.”
Nishiki took a step back. “Oh, shit…! You’re Arakawa’s treasurer? Then that means you’re…”
“Jo Sawashiro,” Sawashiro introduced. “I believe you boys have something that belongs to me.”

Chapter End Notes

This chapter and its follow-up were very fun to do, since it's set earlier than any mainline
Yakuza game. I not only had to imagine what exactly Kiryu and Nishiki would've been doing
in the Dojima Family pre-1988, I also had to sit down and research how a yakuza syndicate
actually functions since this is one of the few times we see the protagonists operate as
members of a yakuza family. I still take some liberties of course for storytelling convenience,
but it was a fun exercise.
As I noted in the comments below, the "Arase" referenced here is NOT Kazuto Arase of the
Nishikiyama family, as he would've been like fourteen in 1986 and to my knowledge was
never a patriarch anyway. The name instead comes from the name of an original character I

created for a potential prequel to this story, with Kiryu as one of two protagonists and set
between Yakuza 6 and Gaiden! :o
I've written four chapters of that prequel so far and will decide if I want to continue writing it
as I near the end of this one. I don't wanna say much else about it except that it's set entirely in
Tokyo during the Omi Alliance takeover that occurred prior to Yakuza: Like A Dragon and
depicts Kiryu's first "major" mission for the Daidoji Faction.

Chapter 105: Brutal Prototype
Jo Sawashiro of the Arakawa Family stood opposite Kiryu and Nishiki in the Empty Lot, one hand
in his pocket as he brought a lighter to the cigarette in his mouth. He flicked the lighter closed,
pocketed it, and blew out a puff of smoke as he eyed the boys before him.
“So…” he began. “You boys thought you’d snatch up that degenerate’s debt, skim out your cut,
then split what’s left between the families he owes. Is that it?” He chuckled, a small cloud of smoke
coming from his nostrils. “Impressive gambit, I’ll give you that. Seriously. That’ll earn you some
serious cred back at the office.”
He brought his cigarette up to his lips for another drag. He inhaled, then exhaled. “Doesn’t make
you a whole lot of friends outside of it, though.”
“Yeah?” Nishiki said, steeling his nerves despite his internal terror. “And who says we’re trying to
impress you, huh? We got Iori to cough up the debt first. Finders keepers.”
Sawashiro flicked his cigarette away and glared at them. “The world doesn’t work like that.” He
slowly stepped toward them. “I’m a reasonable man, though. How about… you hand over the cash,

Kiryu stood firm, his fists clenching. “Not happening,” he said. “You couldn’t get that debt back.
Neither could anyone else in this town. We did. So we’re walking away with what we earned.

Sawashiro studied him for a moment. “…What’s your name, kid?”

Sawashiro raised an eyebrow. “Kiryu? Ah. One of Shintaro Kazama’s strays.” He glanced at
