Kiryu nodded. “So, Sawashiro. If you really want to let these ‘boys’ embarrass you on family
business… then step up!”
Sawashiro turned fully to face them. There was a look in Kiryu’s eyes that he couldn’t quite place.
Steely, fiery resolve. He looked powerful. Composed. Certain.
He looked… like a dragon in the making.
And Sawashiro had always wanted to slay a dragon. He loosened his shoulders, cracked his neck,
and held up his fists. “Hmph. You boys aren’t cowards. I respect that. Let’s see if you can back up
your words, though.”

Kiryu attacked first, running at Sawashiro and throwing a right hook at him; the older yakuza
skillfully dodged this and threw a roundhouse kick at Kiryu’s head in retaliation, which stunned.
Sawashiro then attacked him with a left jab, a right cross, and a right uppercut, the final of which
launched Kiryu in the air.
“Ngh!” Kiryu grunted as he fell on his face, though he quickly stood up despite the pain.
Sawashiro had turned to Nishiki and threw a series of jabs and crosses, all of which hit their mark,
though Nishiki quickly retaliated with his own boxing combo, hitting Sawashiro several times as he
bobbed around, finishing with a flying knee strike. “You little…!” Sawashiro grunted.
Kiryu assisted his oath brother with a right hook, left hook, right upper cut, left kick, and a right
haymaker finisher. He kept the momentum going with a heavy right kick, a left hook, and a flying
right kick, which knocked Sawashiro down.
Bruised but undeterred, Sawashiro swept both boys’ legs, sending them falling to the ground; he
then quickly stood up and stomped on Kiryu’s face, causing him to groan in pain as his nose began
to bleed. Nishiki stood up, and Sawashiro hit him with his basic combo, launching him with the
uppercut and keeping him in the air with several successive hits.
His focus on this task prevented him from noticing that Kiryu had stood back up; he ran at
Sawashiro and, with a yell, jumped into the air and hit him in the back with a dropkick which
knocked the man over. He helped Nishiki up, then turned and kicked Sawashiro in the face as he
tried to stand.
The man fell over, next to a trash can. He opened an eye and saw a shard of glass laying next to his
face. That’ll work. He grabbed it with his bare hand, pushed himself up, and slashed at Kiryu, who

quickly dodged backward. Kiryu kicked his hand, sending the glass flying out of it; it flew up and
nicked Sawashiro’s eyebrow.
It would scar.
He threw a punch at Kiryu, who ducked and responded with a swift counter hook which sent
Sawashiro skidding backwards, his soles burning against the pavement. With a growl, Sawashiro
ran at them with one final raised fist.
Kiryu and Nishiki stood firm, side by side, against him as he approached. “Hmph. Ready, Nishiki?”
Kiryu asked.
Nishiki smirked. “You know it, bro.”
Right as Sawashiro was ready to hit them, they both threw sharp jabs to his stomach—Kiryu with
his right fist, Nishiki with his left—which knocked the air out of Sawashiro’s lungs. The pair then

Kiryu smirked as he wiped blood from his own nose. “Hmph. It wasn’t easy, believe me. But when

Sawashiro’s eyes widened, his fingers already brushing up against the handle of a pistol concealed

Okay?”

The pair walked out of the Empty Lot. Sawashiro removed his hand from his gun a moment later.

“Hey,” Kashiwagi snapped, his tone becoming much, much more stern. “That’s not a gift. That’s a
loan. And you two are going to pay back every. Yen.” He held a finger out, his face morphing into a

scowl. “With. Interest.”
Kiryu stood up and bowed. “Of course, Kashiwagi-san.”
Nishiki raised an eyebrow. “I’m almost afraid to ask, but… what’s the interest.”
Kashiwagi eyed him. “I’ll decide later,” he replied after a moment. “There’s going to come a time
when you two will be making millions a week, each,” he continued. “And this amount of money
will mean nothing to you.” He leaned in. “But you’re not at that level yet. So you better appreciate
it. Got that?”
Nishiki nodded. “Yeah. Got it.”
Kashiwagi waved them out. “Now get out of here. And for God’s sake, if you value your

Nishiki grinned. “Yes, of course. Thanks again!” He stood up. “Come Kiryu, let’s get this to Kuzeaniki.”
Kiryu nodded. “Right.”
Kashiwagi raised an eyebrow as the boys moved to the door. “Hey. You… are going to take the

Nishiki furrowed his brow. “…Huh?”
Kashiwagi leaned forward in his seat. “You weren’t going to hand two fresh stacks of bills to Kuze,
tightly bound like they just came out of a vault, and try and tell him you got them from a debt

Nishiki looked down at the bundle in his hand. His face flushed bright red. “Oh! Uh… yeah! No!
Of course not! Hehe…” He laughed nervously and ripped the straps from the bills. Kiryu followed
suit, and they shuffled the money into their envelope meant for Kuze. “We’d have to be TOTAL

Kiryu sighed and shook his head. “Nishiki, let’s just go already.”
Nishiki nodded. “Right.”
With that, they walked out, leaving Kashiwagi sitting in disbelief.

Back in the present, Kiryu continued to stare at Shujin Academy’s gates. For some reason, despite
how stressful that period of his life was, he looked back on it fondly. Nishiki and Yumi… despite

“Yo, Kiryu-san,” he heard Kasuga’s voice in his ear. He turned to face him.
He was standing side by side with Haruka, whose head was tilted in mild concern. “You doin’
alright?” he asked. “You just kinda… zoned out on us.”

Kiryu stared at them. In Haruka, he obviously saw her mother. It was as if Yumi was still here, still

And Kasuga…
He reminded him of someone else too.

Chapter 106: Arakawa no Kyokun
March 4th, 1986
Jo Sawashiro returned to the Arakawa Family’s tiny office in southern Kamurocho, his eyebrow
scarred, his nose broken, and his pride wounded. He was surprised to find Masumi Arakawa sitting
in the captain’s seat as soon as he entered the office, his fedora casting a shadow on his face.
“Evening, Jo,” Arakawa said quietly.
Sawashiro’s eyes widened. “…Boss?” He bowed submissively. “Uh, I mean, evening, boss.”
Arakawa chuckled. “Did I frighten you?”

Arakawa glanced at the door leading into his private office, on the small unit’s western wall. “Yes,

He tilted his head, allowing some light to shine on his cheek, illuminating the large, shallow scar on

I’m sorry.”
Arakawa’s face didn’t shift. He simply leaned back in his seat. “Oh, I’m sure it’s not as serious as
you think. But do tell. And stand up straight. Believe me, all of that bowing will bring hell down on

Sawashiro nodded and straightened out. “As you know, since you assigned me our credit operation,

Arakawa nodded. “Mhmm. I remember he only asked you for a small sum. A hundred thousand

Arakawa nodded his head slightly. “And?”

“…And two… boys from the Dojima Family beat me to the punch on collection. And worst of

Sawashiro froze.
Arakawa’s lip twitched, though not in anger. “The Dojima boys were just here. Gave me this. They

Sawashiro bowed once more. “I’ve failed you, boss.”
Arakawa sighed. “Jo…”
He stood up and slowly walked around the desk, approaching Sawashiro. “Lift your head, Jo.”
He did not.
Arakawa crossed his arms. “That’s an order.”
Sawashiro exhaled and slowly stood up, but he still wouldn’t meet his eyes.
“What is it that you believe your failure was?” Arakawa asked.

Arakawa nodded. “I see. Well… I simply don’t see it that way.”
Sawashiro’s eyes flicked to his boss. “Sir?”
Arakawa shrugged and paced the room. “So you lost a fight. Big deal. It happens all the time. In

Sawashiro nodded. “The Kamuro Shopping District.”

Sawashiro tilted his head. “Which family?”

He shrugged. “But I wouldn’t call it a failure. We lost nothing. We merely didn’t gain. The same

Sawashiro winced. “Ngh…”
“However… it seems as though the boys returned the principal to us. So although we did not gain

He approached the window and looked out at Kamurocho, or what little of it he could see in his

He turned back to Sawashiro and walked towards him. “Tell me… when you looked at those

Sawashiro had to think only a minute. “…Well… One of them… He wasn’t anything special.

Arakawa smiled. “You saw it too, didn’t you? Yes, that boy… He’s an interesting one. He’s

“No, losing to that isn’t a shame at all,” he continued, his voice growing quiet. “The truth is that,

He put a hand on Sawashiro’s shoulder. “Because when a dragon walks… those with the will to

Sawashiro nodded his head solemnly. “Yes, sir. I won’t fail you again.” The next time I face

Arakawa smirked. “Good. Now then… Why don’t you accompany Masato and I for dinner? As
punishment for your loss, you can pick up the check. Hah!”
Sawashiro smirked back at him. “Hmph. I would be honored to treat you and the young master.”
Arakawa nodded and led Sawashiro out the door.

Chapter 107: Dragonfish

Chapter 110: Rolling Eyes Fall Down the Waterfall
The sound of fist on flesh echoed through the parking lot.
Kazuma Kiryu and Ichiban Kasuga stood perfectly still, their muscles tensing but their bodies
refusing to move as each one tanked a punch to the face from the other. Kiryu’s eyes narrowed
slightly, pain flickering behind them. Kasuga’s grin refused to falter, even as he twitched and
grunted.
Finally, Kiryu made the first move, bringing his other fist into an uppercut, which Kasuga quickly
dodged with a backwards hop.
“If you want to die…” Kiryu growled, “…then step up!” It was a phrase he repeated often, usually
to punks who were in way over their heads.
Ichiban Kasuga was his friend, but he was also both of the above.
Ichiban’s vision shifted, his hallucinations kicked in and Kiryu transformed, and the battle had
begun in earnest.
Haruka stood off to the side, hands behind her back, leaning forward in interest, wondering who
she should root for. On one hand, Kiryu raised her, and she spent years rooting for him in fights (a
thought that, she realized, was not indicative of a typical childhood).
On the other hand… Kasuga had sort of earned this, no?
So, she decided, screw it, she’d root for the underdog today.
Just this once.
“Hey, Haruka-chan,” Kasuga said, glancing at her.
“Hm?”
“Don’t even think about backseating, you hear?”
Haruka blinked. “…Excuse me?”
“This here fight’s between me and Kiryu-san,” he said with a chuckle. “And I wanna win fair and

Her eyes drifted to the three cups before her, arranged from smallest to largest. She began to fill

Chapter 114: Disquiet
It’s easier than one would expect to clean blood and brain matter up when the stained surfaces are
all marble.
Or, at least, easier than Kazuki Soma would have thought. Usually he wasn’t around for the
cleanup.
Yet here he stood, in the middle of his ornate new office at the Daidoji Faction temple in Kyoto,
having been fully cleaned up from the… disagreement that led to his promotion.
Two terrified lower-level agents stood across from his desk as he sat behind it, sniffling into his
handkerchief. “Status report,” he demanded. “Have our field agents been recalled for their new
assignments?”
One terrified underling, Hashimoto, nodded. “Y-yes, sir. Everybody is on their way back to Kyoto
now. …N-nearly everyone, that is.”
Soma’s eyes flicked up to him. “…Nearly?”
Hashimoto started to tremble. The agent beside him, Tanaka, swallowed. “W-well… the truth is,
sir… We still haven’t been able to get in touch with two agents. The first is Yoshimura. He was…
next in line to lead, before The Boss’s…”
“Untimely passing?” Soma chuckled.
Tanaka nodded. “Yes. He appears to have gone… completely off the grid.”
Soma’s eyes narrowed. He slowly sniffled into his handkerchief. “And the other agent?”
“Codename: Kage,” Hashimoto said.
Soma blinked.
“Who?”
“W-we don’t know his real name, or even where he might have gone,” Hashimoto sighed. “He’s
not on regular rotation… he’s almost never at the temple. Operates independently, comes and goes
as needed. He’s been at the Faction longer than either of us. But he’s one of Yoshimura’s, we’re
almost certain. The few times we have seen him, he’s been with Yoshimura.”
Soma leaned back in his seat, putting his feet up on the desk, his shoes scuffing the polished wood.
“Useless…” he muttered. “What about Hanawa? Have we located him?”
Tanaka shook his head. “We traced his cellphone to Shibuya. Found it smashed with a hammer in
front of an airsoft shop. His bank account’s been emptied as well. We don’t use rail cards anymore
either, after one of our agents had his travel history traced by a blackmail gang a few years ago;
paper tickets only. He was last captured on CCTV, at Shibuya Station with Kazuma Kiryu. They
may have boarded a train out of Tokyo.”

Soma looked up. “…May have?”
“Well… there’s a blind spot on the platform, you see…”
Soma scoffed. “Of course there is.”
“As a result… we didn’t see what train they got on… if they got on one. And we couldn’t find them
on any of the onboard cameras.”
Soma shook his head. “Well, you know what you need to do, right?”
“…Find th—“
“Burn them,” Soma snapped. “We can’t have rogue assets wandering the country. Find Kazuma
Kiryu. Find Hanawa. Find Chihiro Watanabe. I want examples made of them. Find Yoshimura.
Make sure he can’t interfere. And whoever the fuck this ‘Kage’ is? I want everything you can dig
up.”
He waved a hand dismissively. “Check Yokohama first. Isezaki Ijincho. That’s where Haruka
Sawamura is. It’s likely where Kiryu will be.”
“That’ll be a little difficult, sir…” Hashimoto muttered.
Soma stood up. “Excuse me?”
Hashimoto backed up. “I-it’s just… Ijincho… it’s one of the only places where the Daidoji haven’t
been able to establish operations. The local gangs, they… they’ve taken out several of our
operatives before.”
Soma glared at him… then sighed and sat down. “Unbelievable. Do we have contacts down there?”
“Geomijul,” Tanaka replied. “Korean gangsters.”
Soma nodded. “I’ve worked in their orbit before. Can you get in touch with their leader?”
“Y-yes, but—“
“Well then it sounds like you have a train to catch,” Soma cut him off, cracking his neck with a roll
of his head, “don’t you?”
Hashimoto glanced at Tanaka. “U-us? But, um…”
Soma narrowed his eyes.
Hashimoto’s widened. “Y-yes sir!” He bowed, as did his companion. “We’ll head to Yokohama
right away!”
“B-but that Seonhee bitch is crazy!” Tanaka hissed.
Hashimoto grabbed his shoulder and pulled him away. “Crazier than this guy?” he whispered.
They both turned to look at Soma, who simply smiled thinly at them.
Tanaka sighed. “Good point.”

With that, they left, leaving Soma all alone. With a sigh, he leaned back in his seat and put his feet
back up on the desk, grabbing a remote and flicking on a television screen against the far wall. He
discovered shortly after commandeering this office that the televisions at the temple used a high
powered satellite system to access networks across the country, as well as in other countries where
the CLP had an interest in local affairs. He flicked through channels.
“Kyiv announced today a series of incursions into—.”
Boring.
“—at a state dinner with United States President Joe Lawton—.”
Next.
“—the corruption trial of former Korean President—.”
Predictable.
“—possible removal of Yasoinaba Prefectural Police Chief Ryotaro Dojima should his department
continue not to comply with NPA—”
Isn’t there anything good on?
Finally, he settled on a Tokyo-area news network.
“—grand reopening ceremony of Little Asia in Kamurocho, which is slated for tomorrow. Set to be
present at the ceremony is Tokyo Governor Saori Yoshida, as well as Shinjuku Mayor Kenichi
Yoshizumi, and Tokyo Police Commissioner Akio Yamamoto. Tokyo Deputy Chief Prosecutor Sae
Niijima, who was originally slated to be present, will now no longer be attending. No reason has
been given as to why.”
Soma raised an eyebrow and placed the remote down.
“Uniformed MPD officers, as well as suited men speculated to be Bleach Japan—Yamamoto’s
rehabilitation program for ex-yakuza and other former convicts, focused around community
policing—had been seen leaving her office in Shibuya several nights prior with what appeared to
be seized evidence. The scope of this investigation, and whether or not Niijima herself is a target,
are still unknown. The MPD and the Ministry of Justice have yet to respond to requests for
comment.”
Soma had read an article about these people back in Osaka. “Yamamoto… Ah. Now I remember.
He’s the one who’s been going after Haruka Sawamura.” He smirked. “Perhaps I don’t need to seek
out Kiryu or Hanawa after all. Maybe… I can make them come to me. All I have to do… is find the
right nerve to squeeze.”
His eyes narrowed on an image of Yamamoto as it flashed onto the television. “Akio Yamamoto…
it’s high time I introduce myself.”

Chapter 115: The Empress
Seonhee sat at the bar at Survive, a slight scowl adorning her face. Her shoulders were tense. Her
grip around her glass was tight. She appeared to be stressed about something as she lifted her glass
to her lips and sipped.

Haruka approached the bar with a soft smile on her face. “Seonhee,” she greeted. “Is everything
alright?”
Seonhee glanced at her. “Everything’s fine,” she muttered. “Thanks.”
“Mm… doesn’t look like it,” Haruka replied. “You look stressed.”
“Secret’s out,” Seonhee replied dryly. “Running the most dangerous gang in Yokohama is stressful.
Who could have guessed?”
Haruka sat down next to her. “Do you want to talk about it?”
Seonhee simply stared at her. “…You really are a little too fearless for your own good.”
Kashiwagi snorted from behind the counter. “It’s a learned behavior,” he muttered as he slid a glass

Haruka glanced down at her glass. Clear liquid, but she could smell it was not water. “What’s this?”
“Soju,” Kashiwagi answered. “It’s Korean. Seonhee’s drink of choice, so I keep a bottle behind the
bar. That one is peach.”
Haruka shrugged and took a sip. Her eyes lit up. “Mm. I like it, too. I love peach.”
“That’s because you have good taste,” Seonhee commended.

“If I told you…” Seonhee said, not looking up at her, “…I’d have to kill you.” She glanced up at
Haruka, a dangerous look in her eyes.
Haruka simply smiled at her.

“…You‘re not going to stop asking, are you?”

Mitsuo tilted his head. “S-sir…?”

“Sit,” Arakawa ordered. “I was going to announce this at the next family meeting, but since you’re
here, I may as well tell you. Mitsu… Effective tomorrow… We are Tojo Clan no more.”
Mitsuo’s eyes widened even as he sat. “W…what?”
“I’ve decided to betray our old clan,” Arakawa said, still sounding amused. The casualness in his
voice gave Mitsuo whiplash. “We’ll be joining the Omi Alliance, as the lead organization of its new
Tokyo branch.”
“Surely that’s a joke, sir!”
“It is not,” Daigo said quietly. “It has already been set in motion.”
“But… why?!”
“If you’ll give me a moment,” Arakawa said, “I will explain everything.”
And so he did, and as he did, Mitsuo’s confused and distraught look slowly softened into something
more understanding. Ryo Aoki, the Governor of Tokyo, had approached Arakawa the week prior to
deliver an ultimatum; either betray the Tojo Clan and begin feeding the police information on their
operations so that he may take them down, or else the police will begin arresting members of the
Arakawa Family on trumped up charges, disrupting their business and eventually forcing the family
to dissolve.
“I approached the Sixth Chairman with my dilemma shortly afterwards,” Arakawa said, turning to
Daigo, who nodded.
“And I told him… to do as Ryo Aoki says,” Daigo revealed. “I told Arakawa-san to betray the Tojo
Clan. As we speak, intelligence about our operations is being leaked to the MPD.” He leaned
forward, steepling his fingers. “…The arrests will begin any day now.”
“But… why take it?” Mitsuo asked. “Why not go down fighting? And what does the Omi Alliance
have to do with it?”
Watase looked over at him. “We’ve got problems of our own out east,” he revealed. “Fuckin’
cops’re tearin’ us apart. Every day it’s somethin’ new. One-a my guys gets arrested. One-a my guys

He closed his eyes, a pained expression on his face. “Without the Fourth Chairman as a stabilizing

“Arase was always a fuckin’ rat…” Majima grumbled. “Never liked him.”

“Didn’t matter if you liked him, Majima-san,” Daigo argued. “He was one of the last ones keeping

“See… the Tojo Clan was, supposedly, formed during the war by these men, because despite their

He straightened out and looked at Watase. “So Watase-san and I agreed… that just as the Tojo and

going to dissolve. Together. A Great Dissolution of Japan’s two largest yakuza syndicates.”
Mitsuo nodded slowly. “…So… What’s gonna happen to us?”
“There are ideas,” Arakawa said. “Nothing concrete. But it is my belief that this dissolution cannot

meantime, it is my job to consolidate Tokyo’s yakuza under the Omi Alliance so that when we
dissolve, we all do it together.”
“I see…” Mitsuo said.
He wouldn’t meet Arakawa’s eyes.

“…Who else knows about this?” he asked finally.
Arakawa didn’t flinch. “…Just those in this room.”
“So… nobody else knows what’s about to happen,” Mitsuo muttered. “Nobody else knows… that
it’s all going to come crumbling down.”
Arakawa nodded slowly. “I understand if this upsets you. You have, after all, dedicated your entire
adult life to the Tojo Clan. But this is necessary. Things cannot continue the way they have been. I
only hope that you can find it in your heart to help us see this through, by helping the family
through this transition.”
Mitsuo didn’t say anything, at first. Then… he stood up.
Fists clenched.
Daigo tensed. Majima grinned. Saejima watched with curiosity.
“Boss…” he muttered. “You’re wrong.”
Arakawa raised an eyebrow. “Oh?”
“I didn’t dedicate my life to the Tojo Clan,” he said quietly. “I dedicated it… to you.”
He then bowed deeply.
“I… would be honored to follow you into the Omi Alliance,” he said genuinely. “To help you see
this through. I don’t know if I fully agree with what you all are saying, but… If this is what you
think is best… I’m with you all the way!”

And so with the Arakawa Family did Mitsuo remain through the Great Dissolution. After

And when that came crumbling down as well, he returned to Kamurocho.
There he sat in the back office of Club Emerald Hills, a cabaret club on West Shichifuku Street that

Toru Higashi, who Mitsuo recognized as a former associate of the Matsugane Family—the prior

“…So you see… It’s all about protecting the community,” Hayashi said, smiling thinly. “To give

Mitsuo’s face didn’t shift, although his eyes did flick to Higashi. “…I hear you guys are goin’ after
Ichiban Kasuga,” he said finally. “That true?”
Hayashi frowned. “…Unfortunate business, that. You’ve heard of the Shin Tojo Alliance, yes? It
seems… that poor, stupid Kasuga has gotten himself wrapped up in it. Sweet-talked, I’m sure,

seduced even, by Haruka Sawamura.”
He stood up and paced the room. “I’m sure he thinks he’s doing something good. Giving a home to

Mitsuo’s eyes narrowed.
Slightly.
“…You really think so, huh?” Mitsuo asked.
Hayashi nodded. “Yes. All we want… is to bring Ichiban Kasuga and Masaharu Kaito back to the

Mitsuo glanced at Higashi again.
Slowly… he nodded.
Mitsuo smirked. “Hmph. You know what?” He gripped Hayashi’s hand, causing Higashi to also

Lost.
Dangerous.
Curiously, Haruka tilted her head. Where did he come from? she wondered. He wasn’t here a
moment ago.

Haruka approached the man. “Excuse me, sir.”
The man’s eyes flicked to her. He clearly heard her. He then looked away and took another drag of
his cigarette.
It was filterless. Hand-rolled, by the looks of it.
“…Sir.”
Again, the man tilted his head, as if he heard her, but he continued to ignore her.
“…Mister.”
Finally, hesitantly, the man looked around, an eyebrow raised. There was nobody else around. He
slowly turned to look at Haruka. She could see, even through the dark tint of his sunglasses, that his
eyes were bright blue, yet his facial features were unmistakably Japanese. “…Are you… talking to
me?” he asked.
Haruka tilted her head. “There’s nobody else around, is there?”

His eyes widened. “Huh…? You are talking to me. But that’s…”
“You seem surprised.”
The man stared at her, then shook his head. “It’s nothing.” He took another drag of his cigarette.
Then, in English, he said “There’s no way…”
“No way what?” Haruka asked, also in English.
His head snapped to her, looking even more shocked. “…English?”
“A small amount,” she replied. “In Tokyo, many English speakers. Nihongo better.”
The man nodded, and replied in Japanese, “Japanese it is then.” He took another drag of his
cigarette, which burned down to a nub. “Sorry. I just… have a lot on my mind.” He glanced around.
“I’m not exactly from around here.”
“Not from… Tokyo?” Haruka asked.
“…Not from Japan.” He gestured to his eyes. “As you can see.”
“I can’t tell that just by looking at you,” Haruka said with a slight chuckle. “You look pretty
Japanese to me.”
“News to me.”
“So… American, then?”
The man paused. “…I don’t remember.”
Haruka blinked. “Huh?”
“…I don’t know much about myself,” he admitted. “When I try to think about it I just… draw a
blank. And what I can remember… I don’t even know if I can trust it.”
He has… amnesia? Haruka thought. “…Do you remember your name?”
The man looked around, thinking about it. “…Daito,” he replied. “I think… I think that’s right.”
Haruka smiled and held her hand out. “Well, Daito-san. It’s nice to meet you. My name’s Haruka.”
Daito stared at her hand for a moment. “…Can I ask you something? A favor. Big one.”
“Huh? Uh, what is it?”
“See… There’s… something I need to see,” he said. “I don’t remember what, and I don’t remember
why… but I think it’s tied to my memories. Maybe if I can see it… I’ll remember.” He looked into
her eyes. “I think it’s in Tokyo. That must be why I’m here. I- I’d go see it myself, but… I’m kind
of stuck here.”
Haruka raised an eyebrow. “Stuck here?”
“I need… somebody to take me.” He bowed his head slightly. “I know it’s a lot to ask. But…
Would you let me come with you, so I can see with your eyes?”

“Oh, well, sure, I can show you around.”
Daito stared at her. “…Are you absolutely sure? Because once you agree… you might be stuck
with me for a bit. So… are you sure?”
Haruka chuckled and nodded. “I’m sure, Daito-san. I’ll help you however I can.”
Daito stared a moment longer, then bowed his head gratefully. “Thank you, Haruka. You don’t
know how much this means to me.”
With that, he held out his hand, and Haruka shook it. Suddenly, she felt a cold breeze come over
her. She shuddered. “…Sheesh. Let’s get moving… It feels really cold all of a sudden.”
Daito nodded and let go of her hand. “Yes. Let’s go.”
They started to walk in the opposite direction of the subway. Strangely, her feet seemed to move on
their own. “Although… I’m not exactly from Tokyo either, so I don’t know how much help I’ll be.”
Daito chuckled. “Then we’re both strangers in heaven,” he said.
“Heh. Yeah.”
From down the sidewalk, Kasuga watched Haruka go, an eyebrow raised. “Haruka-chan…?”

Chapter 139: Stranger Than Heaven
Chapter Notes

This chapter has substory music. ...Yeah.

Haruka and Daito walked through the city, almost directionless. “So… You said you aren’t from
Tokyo,” Daito said. “Where are you from?”
“Well, I was born in Tokyo, I guess…” she admitted. “But it’s not really home to me. I’ve spent
most of my life in Okinawa, with my foster brothers and sisters, and my son.”
“Ah, you’re an orphan too, then?” he asked.
“Huh? Yeah. You too?”
Daito paused. “…I guess. I said it, didn’t I?”
“Yeah. Is… a memory coming back to you?”
Daito shook his head. “More like… it feels true. Like my name. …Memory is funny like that, I
guess.”
“Does anything else feel true?”
Daito hummed and crossed his arms. “…Hm. No. Not yet.”
“Well, once we get to Hachikocho, maybe we can jog some more memories loose?”
“…Hachikocho? Where’s that, exactly?”
“It’s a district in Shibuya.”
Daito put a finger to his chin. “…Can’t say I ever spent much time in Shibuya… I remember things
being… bad there.”
Haruka raised an eyebrow. Are we talking about the same Shibuya…?
As they got closer to Shibuya, Daito seemed to… stare at the tall buildings surrounding them. Like
he was taking them in. “…Where were we just now?”
“Huh?”

“I mean… the hospital. Where was that?”
“Oh! Shinjuku.” She smiled. “When you look at pictures of Tokyo online and you see all the tall
buildings, usually that’s Shinjuku you’re looking at.”
Daito blinked. “On a line? Like… a telephone line?”
Haruka shook her head. “N-not anymore, no.” Sheesh, is dial-up really the last time this guy’s used
the internet?
Meanwhile, Daito’s thoughts were considerably more bizarre. Does this girl really expect me to
believe we can look at photographs on the telephone? He wondered what somebody would even
look at.
As if on cue, he saw a building nearby with a lot of photographs inside, and a man ushering
salarymen in. “Hey, come on, come on in, let me show you what Hachikocho’s got to offer!”
Maybe this will awaken some memories, Daito thought.
Haruka’s brow furrowed. “Um… Daito-san…” she said as he walked directly into the Men’s
Entertainment Box with no shame. The barker seemed to ignore him as he walked in, which
Haruka thought was peculiar. Haruka walked up to the door, and the barker’s eyes widened. “Um,
miss, you’re—.”
“Assisting a friend,” Haruka replied flatly. Her eyes drifted to a rather attractive looking woman on
a photograph inside the MEB. “…And that’s it,” she added, somewhat less convincingly.
“O…kay then,” the barker replied. “Yeah, I mean… It’s 2022. I’m sure we’ve got some girls that
swing that way.”
“Way more than you think,” Haruka replied.
“…’Scuse me?”
“…Nothing.” She walked into the box, following Daito, who was staring wide-eyed at all of the
photos.
“…Wow,” he muttered.
Every single picture in the establishment, of which there were hundreds, was a polished,
professionally shot photo of a different beautiful woman, who came in all sorts of shapes and sizes.
Daito was blown away. “What is this magical place?” he asked.
“It’s a Men’s Entertainment Box,” Haruka explained. “These photos are all of, um, hostesses at the
nearby cabaret clubs. It’s kind of like… a showroom.” She stared at one photo of a woman with
long, dark brown hair in a stunning white Victorian-inspired dress. According to the card in front of
the photo, her name was Sumire and she worked at Sunshine Tokyo, the Shibuya branch of a
famous Sotenbori cabaret club.
For some reason, the name and address of the club embedded itself in Haruka’s memory. She
slowly closed her eyes. I’m not going there. I’m not going there. I’m not going there. Cabaret clubs
are for perverted men. Also I don’t have the money. I’m not going there.

“…Say Daito-san, do you think your memories might be in one of these cabaret clubs?”
Daito stared at one photo - of a hostess with a polite smile named “Moeka” - and frowned slightly.
“...I don’t think so.”
“Right…”
Daito glanced at her. “...You sound disappointed.”
“I’m not.”
“Heh. Okay.” Staring back down at the photo of Moeka, he tilted his head. “Although…”
Suddenly, three images flashed in his mind. Memories? The first was of a young woman with tired
eyes and black hair, pulled up in a bun. She wore a kimono and sat with him at a bar of some sort,
holding a whiskey highball in her hand and staring longingly at him. “Come over here…”
The second was of an American woman with tan skin and curly, shoulder-length brown hair,
standing behind a microphone in a dimly lit club. “Remember my promise… yeah?”
The third was of a Japanese woman with wavy, chin-length black hair in a stylish blue dress and
black gloves, with pearls around her neck and a blue flower in her hair, singing for an adoring
crowd of people in a cabaret. She winked up at Daito, who watched from a balcony. “Something
wrong there, boss?”
Daito snapped back to reality and blinked, clutching his head. Haruka noticed.
“Are you okay, Daito-san?”
Daito took a deep breath… and nodded. “…Yeah.” Looking back down at Moeka’s photo, he added
“I just remembered somebody, is all.”
“Oh? Somebody important?”
“I think… maybe.” He shook his head. “Three women. Couldn’t tell you their names, though.”
“Lovers?”
Daito thought about it. “Maybe. Or… maybe not. I find it hard to believe somebody could love
me.”
“Why is that?”
Daito tilted his head. “…Just another thing I know, I guess. I remember… screaming. People
looking at me like I was some kind of… monster.” He looked sad. “…What did I do…?”
A voice echoed in his mind. A Japanese woman’s voice. “I don’t even know you anymore… I don’t
know what you’ve become.”
Daito slowly closed his eyes. “…We should go.”
Without another word, he turned and walked out of the establishment. Haruka watched him go, a
worried look on her face.

Once again, the barker ignored Daito.

Haruka and Daito soon reached Hachikocho proper, finding themselves in Station Square. He
looked around the area. “…Where is this?” he asked incredulously, staring across the bigass
intersection at the bigass buildings with the bigass LED screens and brightass lights.
Haruka tilted her head. “What do you mean? It’s Shibuya.”
“This is not Shibuya.”
Haruka crossed her arms. “How can you say that? You don’t remember anything.”
“Yeah, certainly not this. Shibuya doesn’t look like this in my memories.”
“Well what does it look like?”
“Rubble.”
Haruka blinked. “…Rubble???”
Daito nodded. “Yeah. Rubble over there, and over there, and where that big building with the
numbers on it is…”
“Daito-san, are you sure you aren’t remembering an old war movie?”
Daito thought about it. “Now that I think about it… I remember war. And I remember movies.
Although, I don’t remember any movies about the war. I mostly watched samurai films. But I will

Haruka tilted her head. “Who?”
Daito looked scandalized. “Sanshiro Sugata?”
Haruka blinked. “…The… The SEGA Saturn mascot?”
“Sega?” Daito asked. Ah. Service Games. This girl is an addict. Poor thing. His eyes flicked to a

Where the hell could that be? Haruka thought to herself. “…Are you even from Tokyo?”
